      {
        "tool_use_id": "toolu_0136RnkJZLHVxETWcX4HoeQY",
        "type": "tool_result",
        "content": "# Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets\n\nThis repository measures how long basic operations on links take in two\ndatabases:\n\n- **Neo4j** 2026.09 Community Edition with default settings, used from Rust\n  through the [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs) Bolt driver;\n- **Doublets**, the [doublets](https://crates.io/crates/doublets) Rust\n  library from LinksPlatform, used in the same process as the benchmark.\n\nA link (doublet) is a triple `(id, source, target)`. Both databases implement\nthe same [`Doublets`](https://docs.rs/doublets) interface, and every benchmark\ncalls the same methods on all of them.\n\nThe measured value is the time until an operation is finished from the point\nof view of the caller. Two workloads are reported:\n\n- **One operation per call**: every link operation is a separate call through\n  the `Doublets` interface, as an application calls it one at a time.\n- **Batch** (Neo4j only): the same operations of an iteration are sent to\n  Neo4j as one list in one Cypher statement, so the fixed cost of a statement\n  (round trips, query planning, commit) is paid once per iteration instead of\n  once per operation. Doublets has no batch calls; its batch work is the same\n  sequence of function calls as in the first workload.\n\n## What is compared\n\n| Implementation                | Where the data is                          | A finished operation is                            |\n|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `Doublets_United_Volatile`    | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n| `Doublets_United_NonVolatile` | memory-mapped file                         | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n| `Doublets_Split_Volatile`     | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n| `Doublets_Split_NonVolatile`  | two memory-mapped files                    | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n| `Neo4j_NonTransaction`        | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: every statement is its own transaction  |\n| `Neo4j_Transaction`           | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one explicit transaction per iteration  |\n| `Neo4j_Batch`                 | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one statement with all `N` operations   |\n\n- **United** and **Split** are two Doublets storage layouts: link data and\n  index trees in one array, or in two separate arrays.\n- Neo4j can only be reached over the network, so every Neo4j operation\n  includes at least one round trip to the server. Doublets has no server: its\n  operations are function calls on the process memory. The comparison\n  therefore shows the cost of each way of storing links as it is used, not the\n  cost of the storage engines alone.\n- Neo4j writes every commit to its transaction log on disk. The Doublets stores\n  do not call `fsync`.\n\n## Operations\n\n| Operation     | `Doublets` method            | Neo4j (Cypher, one statement)                              | Doublets                                     |\n|---------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|\n| Create        | `create_point()`             | `CREATE (:Link {id: $id, source: $id, target: $id})`       | write the link, insert it into both trees    |\n| Update        | `update(id, source, target)` | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) ... SET l.source = ..., l.target = ...` | remove from both trees, write, insert  |\n| Delete        | `delete(id)`                 | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) ... DELETE l`                    | remove from both trees, mark as free         |\n| Each All      | `each([*, *, *])`            | `MATCH (l:Link) RETURN ...`                                | scan the array                               |\n| Each Identity | `each_by([id, *, *])`        | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.id = $id RETURN ...`               | read array element `id`                      |\n| Each Concrete | `each_by([*, source, target])` | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.source = $source AND l.target = $target RETURN ...` | search the `(source, target)` tree |\n| Each Outgoing | `each_by([*, source, *])`    | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.source = $source RETURN ...`       | walk the `(source, target)` tree             |\n| Each Incoming | `each_by([*, *, target])`    | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.target = $target RETURN ...`       | walk the `(target, source)` tree             |\n\nIn Neo4j a link is a node `(:Link {id, source, target})`. A link is found by\nits `id` property, which has a uniqueness constraint and therefore an index;\n`source` and `target` have indexes too. The internal node id (`elementId`) is\nnot used as the link id, because Neo4j chooses it itself and may reuse it,\nwhile link ids are chosen by the caller. Update and Delete are single\nstatements that also return the previous `source` and `target`, which the\n`Doublets` interface reports.\n\n`Neo4j_Batch` sends the `N` operations of an iteration as a list parameter\nand runs them with `UNWIND`, for example\n`UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l`. Neo4j finds each link of\nthe list with the same index seek as the single statement. Update is two\nstatements (to `(0, 0)` and back), every other operation one. Each All is\nalready one statement, so it has no batch variant.\n\nThe exact statements and data structures are documented in\n[`rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs`](rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs) and\n[`rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`](rust/src/doublets_impl.rs).\n\n## Method\n\n- `B` (background links) point links `1..=B` exist before every iteration, so\n  the indexes have a realistic size.\n- One iteration performs `N` (links per iteration) operations:\n\n  | Benchmark     | One iteration                                                  |\n  |---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|\n  | Create        | creates `N` links (ids `B + 1..=B + N`)                        |\n  | Update        | `N` × (`update(id, 0, 0)` and `update(id, id, id)`) = `2N` updates |\n  | Delete        | deletes links `B` down to `B - N + 1`                          |\n  | Each All      | one query that returns all `B` links                           |\n  | Each Identity, Each Concrete, Each Outgoing, Each Incoming | `N` queries, for ids `1..=N`, each returning one link |\n\n- The measured time of an iteration starts before the transaction begins and\n  ends after it is committed (for `Neo4j_Transaction`). After the measurement\n  the changes of the iteration are undone (Create is undone by deleting the\n  created links, Delete by creating them again), so every iteration starts\n  from the same links. The undo is not measured.\n- The background links are created once per benchmark and are not measured.\n- [Criterion.rs](https://github.com/bheisler/criterion.rs) collects the\n  samples: 10 samples (at least 5 s) for Neo4j, 100 samples for Doublets. The\n  tables show the median time of one iteration.\n- The CI runs the Neo4j and Doublets benchmarks in separate GitHub Actions jobs\n  (separate virtual machines), and each number of background links in its own\n  job, so they do not compete for the same CPU. Neo4j runs in the official\n  `neo4j:2026.09-community` Docker image without configuration changes.\n- Before the benchmarks, a test checks that all six implementations return the\n  same results and that undoing an iteration restores the links\n  ([`rust/tests/same_behavior.rs`](rust/tests/same_behavior.rs)).\n\nBenchmarks on the main branch use `N = 1,000` and `B` = 10,000, 100,000 and\n1,000,000; such a run takes about 12 minutes on GitHub Actions (the longest\njob, Neo4j with 1,000,000 background links, about 11 minutes). Pull requests\nrun a quick check with `N = 100` and `B = 1,000`. Larger `B` are not possible\nwith doublets 0.5.0 (see [Limitations](#limitations)). Changes that do not\ntouch the code, such as this README, start no tests or benchmarks.\n\n## Results\n\nThe results below are generated by the CI on every change of the benchmark\ncode on the main branch.\n\n<!-- results:start -->\n### 10,000 background links, 1,000 links per iteration\n\nMedian time of one iteration in nanoseconds. The\n  [`neo4j`](https://crates.io/crates/neo4j) crate, which follows the API of the\n  official drivers, needs 2 and 1 because it sends several Bolt messages at\n  once ([`experiments`](experiments)). Neo4j does not publish an official Rust\n  driver.\n- **One client.** The benchmarks run operations one after another from one\n  thread. Throughput with concurrent clients is not measured.\n- **Only time is measured.** Memory use and disk I/O are not collected.\n- **Each Concrete** returns at most one link in Doublets, which treats a\n  `(source, target)` pair as unique; the benchmarks never create two links\n  with the same pair.\n- **At most 1,040,383 links.** The doublets 0.5.0 stores panic when link\n  number 1,040,384 is created: after growing their memory, they use only the\n  newly added part of it as the whole array (see\n  [`experiments/store-capacity`](experiments/store-capacity) and the\n  \"Capacity\" section of [`rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`](rust/src/doublets_impl.rs)).\n  This is why `B` stops at 1,000,000.\n- **Point links only.** The doublets 0.5.0 Split store does not find links\n  with `source != target` by `[*, source, *]` and `[*, source, target]` queries\n  after an `update` (see\n  [`experiments/split-store-bug`](experiments/split-store-bug)). The\n  benchmarks only use point links and links updated to `(0, 0)` and back, for\n  which all stores return the same results.\n- Results before [issue #15](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/issues/15)\n  were measured with an HTTP client that opened a new connection for every\n  request and are not comparable with the current results.\n\n## Running locally\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name neo4j -p 7687:7687 -e NEO4J_AUTH=neo…ord neo4j:2026.09-community\n\ncd rust\ncargo test --release -- --include-ignored     #     "stdout": "# Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets\n\nThis repository measures how long basic operations on links take in two\ndatabases:\n\n- **Neo4j** 2026.09 Community Edition with default settings, used from Rust\n  through the [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs) Bolt driver;\n- **Doublets**, the [doublets](https://crates.io/crates/doublets) Rust\n  library from LinksPlatform, used in the same process as the benchmark.\n\nA link (doublet) is a triple `(id, source, target)`. Both databases implement\nthe same [`Doublets`](https://docs.rs/doublets) interface, and every benchmark\ncalls the same methods on all of them.\n\nThe measured value is the time until an operation is finished from the point\nof view of the caller. Two workloads are reported:\n\n- **One operation per call**: every link operation is a separate call through\n  the `Doublets` interface, as an application calls it one at a time.\n- **Batch** (Neo4j only): the same operations of an iteration are sent to\n  Neo4j as one list in one Cypher statement, so the fixed cost of a statement\n  (round trips, query planning, commit) is paid once per iteration instead of\n  once per operation. Doublets has no batch calls; its batch work is the same\n  sequence of function calls as in the first workload.\n\n## What is compared\n\n| Implementation                | Where the data is                          | A finished operation is                            |\n|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `Doublets_United_Volatile`    | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n| `Doublets_United_NonVolatile` | memory-mapped file                         | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n| `Doublets_Split_Volatile`     | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n| `Doublets_Split_NonVolatile`  | two memory-mapped files                    | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n| `Neo4j_NonTransaction`        | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: every statement is its own transaction  |\n| `Neo4j_Transaction`           | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one explicit transaction per iteration  |\n| `Neo4j_Batch`                 | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one statement with all `N` operations   |\n\n- **United** and **Split** are two Doublets storage layouts: link data and\n  index trees in one array, or in two separate arrays.\n- Neo4j can only be reached over the network, so every Neo4j operation\n  includes at least one round trip to the server. Doublets has no server: its\n  operations are function calls on the process memory. The comparison\n  therefore shows the cost of each way of storing links as it is used, not the\n  cost of the storage engines alone.\n- Neo4j writes every commit to its transaction log on disk. The Doublets stores\n  do not call `fsync`.\n\n## Operations\n\n| Operation     | `Doublets` method            | Neo4j (Cypher, one statement)                              | Doublets                                     |\n|---------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|\n| Create        | `create_point()`             | `CREATE (:Link {id: $id, source: $id, target: $id})`       | write the link, insert it into both trees    |\n| Update        | `update(id, source, target)` | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) ... SET l.source = ..., l.target = ...` | remove from both trees, write, insert  |\n| Delete        | `delete(id)`                 | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) ... DELETE l`                    | remove from both trees, mark as free         |\n| Each All      | `each([*, *, *])`            | `MATCH (l:Link) RETURN ...`                                | scan the array                               |\n| Each Identity | `each_by([id, *, *])`        | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.id = $id RETURN ...`               | read array element `id`                      |\n| Each Concrete | `each_by([*, source, target])` | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.source = $source AND l.target = $target RETURN ...` | search the `(source, target)` tree |\n| Each Outgoing | `each_by([*, source, *])`    | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.source = $source RETURN ...`       | walk the `(source, target)` tree             |\n| Each Incoming | `each_by([*, *, target])`    | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.target = $target RETURN ...`       | walk the `(target, source)` tree             |\n\nIn Neo4j a link is a node `(:Link {id, source, target})`. A link is found by\nits `id` property, which has a uniqueness constraint and therefore an index;\n`source` and `target` have indexes too. The internal node id (`elementId`) is\nnot used as the link id, because Neo4j chooses it itself and may reuse it,\nwhile link ids are chosen by the caller. Update and Delete are single\nstatements that also return the previous `source` and `target`, which the\n`Doublets` interface reports.\n\n`Neo4j_Batch` sends the `N` operations of an iteration as a list parameter\nand runs them with `UNWIND`, for example\n`UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l`. Neo4j finds each link of\nthe list with the same index seek as the single statement. Update is two\nstatements (to `(0, 0)` and back), every other operation one. Each All is\nalready one statement, so it has no batch variant.\n\nThe exact statements and data structures are documented in\n[`rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs`](rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs) and\n[`rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`](rust/src/doublets_impl.rs).\n\n## Method\n\n- `B` (background links) point links `1..=B` exist before every iteration, so\n  the indexes have a realistic size.\n- One iteration performs `N` (links per iteration) operations:\n\n  | Benchmark     | One iteration                                                  |\n  |---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|\n  | Create        | creates `N` links (ids `B + 1..=B + N`)                        |\n  | Update        | `N` × (`update(id, 0, 0)` and `update(id, id, id)`) = `2N` updates |\n  | Delete        | deletes links `B` down to `B - N + 1`                          |\n  | Each All      | one query that returns all `B` links                           |\n  | Each Identity, Each Concrete, Each Outgoing, Each Incoming | `N` queries, for ids `1..=N`, each returning one link |\n\n- The measured time of an iteration starts before the transaction begins and\n  ends after it is committed (for `Neo4j_Transaction`). After the measurement\n  the changes of the iteration are undone (Create is undone by deleting the\n  created links, Delete by creating them again), so every iteration starts\n  from the same links. The undo is not measured.\n- The background links are created once per benchmark and are not measured.\n- [Criterion.rs](https://github.com/bheisler/criterion.rs) collects the\n  samples: 10 samples (at least 5 s) for Neo4j, 100 samples for Doublets. The\n  tables show the median time of one iteration.\n- The CI runs the Neo4j and Doublets benchmarks in separate GitHub Actions jobs\n  (separate virtual machines), and each number of background links in its own\n  job, so they do not compete for the same CPU. Neo4j runs in the official\n  `neo4j:2026.09-community` Docker image without configuration changes.\n- Before the benchmarks, a test checks that all six implementations return the\n  same results and that undoing an iteration restores the links\n  ([`rust/tests/same_behavior.rs`](rust/tests/same_behavior.rs)).\n\nBenchmarks on the main branch use `N = 1,000` and `B` = 10,000, 100,000 and\n1,000,000; such a run takes about 12 minutes on GitHub Actions (the longest\njob, Neo4j with 1,000,000 background links, about 11 minutes). Pull requests\nrun a quick check with `N = 100` and `B = 1,000`. Larger `B` are not possible\nwith doublets 0.5.0 (see [Limitations](#limitations)). Changes that do not\ntouch the code, such as this README, start no tests or benchmarks.\n\n## Results\n\nThe results below are generated by the CI on every change of the benchmark\ncode on the main branch.\n\n<!-- results:start -->\n### 10,000 background links, 1,000 links per iteration\n\nMedian time of one iteration in nanoseconds. Throughput with concurrent clients is not measured.\n- **Only time is measured.** Memory use and disk I/O are not collected.\n- **Each Concrete** returns at most one link in Doublets, which treats a\n  `(source, target)` pair as unique; the benchmarks never create two links\n  with the same pair.\n- **At most 1,040,383 links.** The doublets 0.5.0 stores panic when link\n  number 1,040,384 is created: after growing their memory, they use only the\n  newly added part of it as the whole array (see\n  [`experiments/store-capacity`](experiments/store-capacity) and the\n  \"Capacity\" section of [`rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`](rust/src/doublets_impl.rs)).\n  This is why `B` stops at 1,000,000.\n- **Point links only.** The doublets 0.5.0 Split store does not find links\n  with `source != target` by `[*, source, *]` and `[*, source, target]` queries\n  after an `update` (see\n  [`experiments/split-store-bug`](experiments/split-store-bug)). The\n  benchmarks only use point links and links updated to `(0, 0)` and back, for\n  which all stores return the same results.\n- Results before [issue #15](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/issues/15)\n  were measured with an HTTP client that opened a new connection for every\n  request and are not comparable with the current results.\n\n## Running locally\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name neo4j -p 7687:7687 -e NEO4J_AUTH=neo…ord neo4j:2026.09-community\n\ncd rust\ncargo test --release -- --include-ignored     # check that all stores agree\ncargo bench --bench bench                     # both databases\nBENCHMARK_BACKEND=doublets cargo bench --bench bench   # Doublets only, no server needed\n```\n\n| Так и должна работать embedded/in-process штука.\n\n---\n\n🔴 А теперь Neo4j\n\nЛогично было бы взять официальный Neo4j driver, Bolt, открыть соединение один раз и гонять запросы через connection pool.\n\nНо тогда цифры, видимо, получились бы недостаточно праздничными.\n\nПоэтому в benchmark написан собственный клиент.\n\nИ для каждой операции он делает:\n\n\"TcpStream::connect()\"\n\nТо есть открывает новое TCP-соединение.\n\nПотом:\n\n\"HTTP → JSON → Cypher → Neo4j → auto-commit → JSON → HTTP\"\n\nПотом читает response.\n\nА потом…\n\n\"Connection: close\"\n\nДа.\n\nАвтор буквально попросил HTTP закрывать соединение после каждого запроса.\n\nПосле чего следующая операция снова начинается с:\n\n\"TcpStream::connect()\".\n\nЭто не overhead, случайно попавший в benchmark.\n\nЭто overhead, заботливо выращенный вручную.\n\n---\n\n🤡 Но подождите, там же написано \"bolt://localhost:7687\"?\n\nДа!\n\nЭто отдельная прекрасная деталь.\n\nСмотришь конфигурацию — видишь:\n\n\"bolt://localhost:7687\"\n\nДумаешь: ну значит используется Bolt.\n\nХуй там плавал.\n\nРеализация берёт этот адрес, идёт на HTTP port 7474 и руками отправляет HTTP-запросы в Neo4j.\n\nТо есть официальный Neo4j driver и Bolt в этом великолепном состязании вообще не участвуют.\n\n---\n\n🏆 Update заслуживает отдельной премии\n\nДопустим, хотим обновить один link.\n\nDoublets:\n\n\"update(link)\"\n\nNeo4j benchmark:\n\nОткрываем TCP connection.\n\nОтправляем HTTP + JSON + Cypher:\n\n\"MATCH ... RETURN source, target\"\n\nПолучаем JSON.\n\nДесериализуем.\n\nЗакрываем соединение.\n\nПотом…\n\nоткрываем новое TCP-соединение.\n\nОтправляем второй HTTP + JSON + Cypher:\n\n\"MATCH ... SET source=..., target=...\"\n\nNeo4j выполняет запрос.\n\nCommit.\n\nJSON.\n\nHTTP.\n\nЗакрываем соединение.\n\nИ теперь сравниваем всё это с локальным вызовом функции.\n\nScience! 🔬\n\n---\n\n🗑 С Delete аналогично\n\nОдин logical delete превращается в:\n\nrequest #1: прочитать link\nrequest #2: удалить link\n\nКаждый со своим:\n\n\"TCP → HTTP → JSON → Cypher → transaction → JSON → HTTP → close\"\n\nПосле чего удивляемся:\n\n«Почему же локальная структура данных быстрее?»\n\nЗагадка века.\n\n---\n\n🚀 И вот рождается 37 000×\n\nВ README получаем что-то вроде:\n\nDoublets Create: ~85 μs\nNeo4j Create: ~3.1 s\n\nИ красивый вывод:\n\n«36 000+ TIMES FASTER 🚀🚀🚀»\n\nТехнически числа могут быть абсолютно настоящими.\n\nПросто benchmark отвечает не на вопрос:\n\n««Насколько storage engine Doublets быстрее Neo4j?»»\n\nОн отвечает на вопрос:\n\n««Насколько прямой вызов специализированной структуры данных в своём процессе быстрее тысячи отдельных HTTP-запросов к отдельному DBMS, каждый из которых открывает TCP connection, сериализует JSON, парсит Cypher, выполняет транзакцию и закрывает connection?»»\n\nОтвет:\n\nОчень.\n\nСпасибо, benchmark.\n\n---\n\n🧪 Это как сравнить \"HashMap.get()\" с \"curl\"\n\nПредставьте benchmark:\n\n\"HashMap.get(key)\"\n\nVS\n\n\"curl http://database/query\"\n\nНо перед каждым \"curl\" мы ещё обязательно устанавливаем новое соединение.\n\nПотом объявляем:\n\n«HASHMAP DESTROYS DATABASE: 25,000X PERFORMANCE 🚀»\n\nФормально — всё измерили правильно.\n\nСодержательно — цирк.\n\n---\n\n☝️ Причём Doublets может быть реально очень быстрой штукой\n\nИ вот это самое обидное.\n\nСама идея специализированного graph storage primitive интересная.         "type": "tool_result",
        "content": "Fixes #15.\n\n## Goal\n\nMeasure how long basic link operations take until they are finished, from the point of view of the caller, in:\n\n- Neo4j 2026.09 Community with default settings (official `neo4j:2026.09-community` Docker image, no configuration changes), used through the neo4rs Bolt driver;\n- the four Doublets stores (United/Split × Volatile/NonVolatile), used in the benchmark process.\n\nTwo workloads are reported separately, as suggested in [the issue discussion](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/issues/15#issuecomment-5982339792):\n\n1. **One operation per call** (`Neo4j_NonTransaction`, `Neo4j_Transaction`, all Doublets columns): every link operation is one call of the `Doublets` interface.\n2. **Batch** (`Neo4j_Batch`): the `N` operations of an iteration are sent to Neo4j as one list in one `UNWIND` statement, so the round trips, planning and commit are paid once per iteration. Doublets has no batch calls, so its numbers are the same in both workloads.\n\nAdditional metrics (RAM, disk I/O, percentiles) are not part of this change. The README lists them as not measured; they can be added later as a separate report.\n\n## What changed in the method\n\n| Before | Now |\n|---|---|\n| Own HTTP client, a new TCP connection for every request, `Connection: close` | [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs) 0.8 Bolt driver with default settings. Its connection pool is opened once and reused by all operations. |\n| Some operations sent two requests (an extra `MATCH` before `SET`/`DELETE`) | Every operation is one Cypher statement. Update and Delete return the previous `source`/`target` from the same statement. |\n| \"Transaction\" mode was not a real Neo4j transaction | `Neo4j_Transaction`: one explicit Bolt transaction per iteration, timed from `begin` to `commit`. `Neo4j_NonTransaction`: every statement is its own auto-commit transaction. |\n| No batch workload | `Neo4j_Batch`: `UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l` and the same for Create, Update and the four `each_by` queries. `EXPLAIN` shows the same index seek per list element as the single statement. |\n| Background links were created again, one request per link, before every iteration, and deleted after it | Background links are created once per benchmark in batches (`UNWIND` + `CALL { ... } IN TRANSACTIONS OF 10000 ROWS`). The changes of an iteration are undone after the measurement, so every iteration starts from the same `B` links. Neither step is measured. |\n| Neo4j and Doublets ran in one job on one VM | Separate GitHub Actions jobs per backend and per `B` |\n\nThe official Neo4j drivers do not include Rust. neo4rs is the Bolt driver maintained in `neo4j-labs` and was accepted in the issue discussion. Its latest stable release is 0.8.0 (0.9 is only a release candidate).\n\n**\"Is it impossible to find a link by id in Neo4j?\"** No. A link is the node `(:Link {id, source, target})`, and it is found by the `id` property through the index of the uniqueness constraint. The internal `elementId` is not used as the link id, because Neo4j chooses it itself and may reuse it, while the caller chooses link ids. This is documented in the README and in `rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs`.\n\n## Code structure\n\n- `rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs`: `Doublets` implementation on top of neo4rs, plus the batch methods (`create_points_batch`, `update_batch`, `delete_batch`, `each_by_batch`). It documents every Cypher statement.\n- `rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`: documents the data structures of the Doublets stores and their capacity.\n- `rust/src/benched/`: setup, fork (background links) and undo for every implementation.\n- `rust/benches/`: one generic benchmark per operation, run by Criterion with `iter_custom`, so only the operations are timed; `benches/benchmarks/neo4j/batch.rs` holds the batch workload.\n- `rust/out.py`: generates the README tables and the charts in `Docs/` from the bencher output.\n- The old HTTP client (`client.rs`, `transaction.rs`, `exclusive.rs`) is removed.\n\n## Toolchain and dependencies\n\n- Latest stable Rust (`rust-toolchain.toml`: `stable`, 1.98.1 at the time of writing), edition 2024. `rustfmt.toml` had only nightly options and is removed; [`Neo4j`] implements the same [`Doublets`] interface as the Doublets stores,\n//! so every benchmark calls exactly the same methods on both databases.\n//!\n//! ## Driver and connection\n//!\n//! Neo4j is reached through [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs),\n//! the Bolt driver maintained by Neo4j Labs. Neo4j does not publish an\n//! official Rust driver.\n//!\n//! - The connection pool is opened once in [`Neo4j::connect`] and reused by\n//!   all operations, so no TCP connection is opened per operation.\n//! - All settings of the driver and of the server are defaults.\n//!\n//! ## Data model\n//!\n//! A link is a node with three integer properties:\n//!\n//! ```cypher\n//! (:Link {id: Integer, source: Integer, target: Integer})\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Links are found by the `id` property, which is backed by a uniqueness\n//! constraint (and therefore by an index). The internal node id (`elementId`)\n//! is not used, because Neo4j assigns it itself and may reuse it after a node\n//! is deleted, while a link id must be chosen by the caller and stay stable.\n//!\n//! ```cypher\n//! CREATE CONSTRAINT link_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) REQUIRE l.id IS UNIQUE\n//! CREATE INDEX link_source IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.source)\n//! CREATE INDEX link_target IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.target)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ## One statement per operation\n//!\n//! | Operation      | Cypher                                                                        |\n//! |----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | `create_point` | `CREATE (:Link {id: $id, source: $id, target: $id})`                          |\n//! | `update`       | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) WITH l, l.source AS source, l.target AS target SET l.source = $new_source, l.target = $new_target RETURN source, target` |\n//! | `delete`       | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) WITH l, l.source AS source, l.target AS target DELETE l RETURN source, target` |\n//! | `each_by`      | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN l.id AS id, l.source AS source, l.target AS target` |\n//! | `count_by`     | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN count(l) AS count`                 |\n//!\n//! `update` and `delete` return the previous `source` and `target` from the\n//! same statement, because the [`Doublets`] interface reports the link state\n//! before and after each change.\n//!\n//! New ids come from a counter kept by the client, as with a database\n//! sequence: `1, 2, 3, ...`. Doublets also assigns `1, 2, 3, ...` to the links\n//! of an empty store. As in Doublets, deleting the link with the highest id\n//! makes that id the next one to be created. Ids of other deleted links are not\n//! reused (Doublets reuses them too); the benchmarks only delete the links with\n//! the highest ids, so both databases always assign the same ids.\n//!\n//! ## Batches\n//!\n//! The `Neo4j_Batch` benchmarks send the parameters of all `N` operations of\n//! an iteration as one list, so the round trips, parsing and planning of a\n//! statement and the commit are paid once per list instead of once per link:\n//!\n//! | Method                | Cypher                                                                        |\n//! |-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | `create_points_batch` | `UNWIND range($first, $last) AS id CREATE (:Link {id: id, source: id, target: id})` |\n//! | `update_batch`        | `UNWIND $links AS link MATCH (l:Link {id: link[0]}) SET l.source = link[1], l.target = link[2] RETURN count(l) AS updated` |\n//! | `delete_batch`        | `UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l RETURN count(l) AS deleted` |\n//! | `each_by_batch`       | `UNWIND $queries AS q MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN ...`, `q` holds the constrained parts of one query |\n//!\n//! Neo4j finds every link of a list with the same index seek as the single\n//! statement does. The batch benchmarks use [`Mode::AutoCommit`], so every\n//! statement is one transaction. The Doublets interface has no batch methods,\n//! so these are methods of [`Neo4j`] only.\n//!\n//! ## Transaction modes\n//!\n//! | [`Mode`]                 | What happens                                                         |\n//! |--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | [`Mode::AutoCommit`]     | Every statement is its own transaction, committed by the server.     |\n//! | [`Mode::Transaction`]    | All statements between [`Neo4j::begin`] and [`Neo4j::commit`] run in one explicit transaction. |\n//!\n//! Errors returned by Neo4j are never ignored: methods that return `Result`\n//! return them as [`Error::Other`], and methods of the [`Links`] trait that\n//! cannot return an error (`each_links`, `count_links`) panic, which stops the\n//! benchmark.\n\nuse std::{\n    error,\n    sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard},\n};\n\nuse doublets::{\n    Doublets, Error, Link, Links,\n    data::{Flow, LinkReference, LinksConstants, ReadHandler, WriteHandler},\n};\nuse neo4rs::{Graph, Query, Row, Txn, query};\nuse tokio::runtime::Runtime;\n\n/// How statements are grouped into transactions.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Mode {\n    /// Every statement is a separate, automatically committed transaction.\n    AutoCommit,\n    /// Statements run in one explicit transaction until [`Neo4j::commit`].\n    Transaction,\n}\n\n/// A links store kept in a Neo4j database.\npub struct Neo4j<T: LinkReference> {\n    /// Runs the asynchronous driver calls to completion on the calling thread.\n    runtime: Runtime,\n    graph: Graph,\n    mode: Mode,\n    /// The open explicit transaction, used only in [`Mode::Transaction`].\n    transaction: Mutex<Option<Txn>>,\n    constants: LinksConstants<T>,\n    next_id: T,\n}\n\n/// Number of links created or deleted per transaction by\n/// [`Neo4j::create_points`] and [`Neo4j::clear`].\npub const BATCH_SIZE: usize = 10_000;\n\n/// Result of a driver call.\ntype Neo4jResult<T> = Result<T, neo4rs::Error>;\n\nimpl<T: LinkReference> Neo4j<T> {\n    /// Opens the connection pool and creates the schema if it does not exist.\n    pub fn connect(uri: &str, user: &str, password: &str, mode: Mode) -> crate::Result<Self> {\n        let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()\n            .enable_all()\n            .build()?;\n        let graph = runtime.block_on(Graph::new(uri, user, password))?;\n        let store = Self {\n            runtime,\n            graph,\n            mode,\n            transaction: Mutex::new(None),\n            constants: LinksConstants::new(),\n            next_id: T::from_byte(1),\n        };\n        for statement in [\n            \"CREATE CONSTRAINT link_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) REQUIRE l.id IS UNIQUE\",\n            \"CREATE INDEX link_source IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.source)\",\n            \"CREATE INDEX link_target IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.target)\",\n        ] {\n            store.run_auto_commit(query(statement))?;\n        }\n        store.run_auto_commit(query(\"CALL db.awaitIndexes()\"))?;\n        Ok(store)\n    }\n\n    /// Opens the connection described by the `NEO4J_URI`, `NEO4J_USER` and\n    /// `NEO4J_PASSWORD` environment variables (defaults:\n    /// `bolt://localhost:7687`, `neo4j`, `password`).\n    pub fn connect_from_env(mode: Mode) -> crate::Result<Self> {\n        let var = |name, default: &str| std::env::var(name).unwrap_or_else(|_| default.to_owned());\n        Self::connect(\n            &var(\"NEO4J_URI\", \"bolt://localhost:7687\"),\n            &var(\"NEO4J_USER\", \"neo4j\"),\n            &var(\"NEO4J_PASSWORD\", \"password\"),\n            mode,\n        )\n    }\n\n    pub fn mode(&self) -> Mode {\n        self.mode\n    }\n\n    /// Creates `count` point links with the next ids, committing every\n    /// [`BATCH_SIZE`] links, so that millions of links do not have to fit into\n    /// the memory of one transaction.\n    ///\n    /// Used to prepare the background links outside of the measured time.\n    pub fn create_points(&mut self, count: usize) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let first = id_to_i64(self.next_id);\n        let last = first + count as i64 - 1;\n        self.run_auto_commit(\n            query(&format!(\n                \"UNWIND range($first, $last) AS id \\\n                 CALL (id) {{ CREATE (:Link {{id: id, source: id, target: id}}) }} \\\n                 IN TRANSACTIONS OF {BATCH_SIZE} ROWS\"\n            ))\n            .param(\"first\", first)\n            .param(\"last\", last),\n        )?;\n        self.next_id = id_from_i64(last + 1);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Starts an explicit transaction when the store is in [`Mode::Transaction`].\n    pub fn begin(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        if self.mode == Mode::Transaction {\n            let transaction = self.runtime.block_on(self.graph.start_txn())?;\n            *self.transaction() = Some(transaction);\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Commits the explicit transaction started by [`Neo4j::begin`], if any.\n    pub fn commit(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        if let Some(transaction) = self.transaction().take() {\n            self.runtime.block_on(transaction.commit())?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rolls back the open transaction, if any, and deletes all links,\n    /// committing every [`BATCH_SIZE`]    self.run_auto_commit(query(&format!(\n            \"MATCH (l:Link) CALL (l) {{ DELETE l }} IN TRANSACTIONS OF {BATCH_SIZE} ROWS\"\n        )))?;\n        self.next_id = T::from_byte(1);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn transaction(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Option<Txn>> {\n        self.transaction\n            .lock()\n            .expect(\"transaction mutex is poisoned\")\n    }\n\n    fn run_auto_commit(&self, query: Query) -> Neo4jResult<()> {\n        self.runtime.block_on(self.graph.run(query))\n    }\n\n    /// Runs `query` in the open transaction (or as an auto-commit\n    /// transaction) and passes every returned row to `on_row`.\n    // The lock is held only by this thread while `block_on` runs the query on\n    // the store's own single-threaded runtime, so no other task can wait for it.\n    #[allow(clippy::await_holding_lock)]\n    fn fetch(&self, query: Query, mut on_row: impl FnMut(Row)) -> Neo4jResult<()> {\n        self.runtime.block_on(async {\n            match self.transaction().as_mut() {\n                Some(transaction) => {\n                    let mut rows = transaction.execute(query).await?;\n                    while let Some(row) = rows.next(transaction.handle()).await? {\n                        on_row(row);\n                    }\n                }\n                None => {\n                    let mut rows = self.graph.execute(query).await?;\n                    while let Some(row) = rows.next().await? {\n                        on_row(row);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(())\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Runs `query` and returns its rows.\n    fn fetch_all(&self, query: Query) -> Neo4jResult<Vec<Row>> {\n        let mut rows = Vec::new();\n        self.fetch(query, |row| rows.push(row))?;\n        Ok(rows)\n    }\n\n    /// Builds `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE ...` for a doublets query\n    /// (`[]`, `[id]` or `[id, source, target]`, where `any` matches everything).\n    fn match_query(&self, query: &[T], returns: &str) -> Query {\n        let filter = self.filter(query, |part| format!(\"${}\", PARTS[part]));\n        PARTS\n            .iter()\n            .zip(query)\n            .filter(|&(_, &value)| value != self.constants.any)\n            .fold(\n                neo4rs::query(&format!(\"MATCH (l:Link){filter} RETURN {returns}\")),\n                |q, (name, &value)| q.param(name, id_to_i64(value)),\n            )\n    }\n\n    /// Builds the ` WHERE ...` clause with one condition per part of `query`\n    /// that is not `any`; `value(part)` is the Cypher expression the property\n    /// is compared with.\n    fn filter(&self, query: &[T], value: impl Fn(usize) -> String) -> String {\n        let conditions: Vec<_> = PARTS\n            .iter()\n            .zip(query)\n            .enumerate()\n            .filter(|&(_, (_, &part))| part != self.constants.any)\n            .map(|(part, (name, _))| format!(\"l.{name} = {}\", value(part)))\n            .collect();\n        if conditions.is_empty() {\n            String::new()\n        } else {\n            format!(\" WHERE {}\", conditions.join(\" AND \"))\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Batches: one statement for many links (the `Neo4j_Batch` benchmarks)\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Creates the point links with the next `count` ids with one statement.\n    pub fn create_points_batch(&mut self, count: usize) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let first = id_to_i64(self.next_id);\n        let last = first + count as i64 - 1;\n        self.fetch_all(\n            query(\n                \"UNWIND range($first, $last) AS id \\\n                 CREATE (:Link {id: id, source: id, target: id})\",\n            )\n            .param(\"first\", first)\n            .param(\"last\", last),\n        )?;\n        self.next_id = id_from_i64(last + 1);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Sets `source` and `target` of every link in `links` (found by its\n    /// `index`) with one statement.\n    pub fn update_batch(&mut self, links: &[Link<T>]) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let expected = links.len();\n        let links: Vec<_> = links\n            .iter()\n            .map(|link| {\n                [link.index, link.source, link.target]\n                    .map(id_to_i64)\n                    .to_vec()\n            })\n            .collect();\n        let rows = self.fetch_all(\n            query(\n                \"UNWIND $links AS link \\\n                 MATCH (l:Link {id: link[0]}) \\\n                 SET l.source = link[1], l.target = link[2] \\\n                 RETURN count(l) AS updated\",\n            )\n            .param(\"links\", links),\n        )?;\n        expect_count(&rows, \"updated\", expected)\n    }\n\n    /// Deletes the links with the given ids with one statement.\n    pub fn delete_batch(&mut self, ids: &[T]) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let rows = self.fetch_all(\n            query(\n                \"UNWIND $ids AS id \\\n                 MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) \\\n                 DELETE l \\\n                 RETURN count(l) AS deleted\",\n            )\n            .param(\n                \"ids\",\n                ids.iter().copied().map(id_to_i64).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n            ),\n        )?;\n        expect_count(&rows, \"deleted\", ids.len())?;\n        // The same T::from_byte(1) == self.next_id {\n                self.next_id = id;\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Runs all `queries` with one statement and passes every found link to\n    /// `handler`.\n    ///\n    /// All queries must constrain the same parts (for example, all are\n    /// `[*, source, *]`), because they share one `WHERE` clause.\n    pub fn each_by_batch(\n        &self,\n        queries: &[[T; 3]],\n        mut handler: impl FnMut(Link<T>),\n    ) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let Some(first) = queries.first() else {\n            return Ok(());\n        };\n        let any = self.constants.any;\n        if queries\n            .iter()\n            .any(|query| (0..3).any(|part| (query[part] == any) != (first[part] == any)))\n        {\n            return Err(\"all queries of a batch must constrain the same parts\".into());\n        }\n        // Only the constrained parts are sent: `q[0]` is the first of them.\n        let parts: Vec<_> = (0..3).filter(|&part| first[part] != any).collect();\n        let filter = self.filter(first, |part| {\n            let position = parts.iter().position(|&p| p == part);\n            format!(\"q[{}]\", position.expect(\"a constrained part\"))\n        });\n        let queries: Vec<_> = queries\n            .iter()\n            .map(|query| {\n                parts\n                    .iter()\n                    .map(|&part| id_to_i64(query[part]))\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            })\n            .collect();\n        self.fetch(\n            query(&format!(\n                \"UNWIND $queries AS q \\\n                 MATCH (l:Link){filter} \\\n                 RETURN l.id AS id, l.source AS source, l.target AS target\"\n            ))\n            .param(\"queries\", queries),\n            |row| handler(link_from_row(&row)),\n        )?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Names of the parts of a link, in the order of a doublets query.\nconst PARTS: [&str; 3] = [\"id\", \"source\", \"target\"];\n\n/// Checks that the `column` of the single row of `rows` equals `expected`.\nfn expect_count(rows: &[Row], column: &str, expected: usize) -> crate::Result<()> {\n    let count: i64 = rows[0].get(column)?;\n    if count != expected as i64 {\n        return Err(format!(\"{count} links {column}, expected {expected}\").into());\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nimpl<T: LinkReference> Links<T> for Neo4j<T> {\n    fn constants(&self) -> &LinksConstants<T> {\n        &self.constants\n    }\n\n    fn count_links(&self, query: &[T]) -> T {\n        let rows = self\n            .fetch_all(self.match_query(query, \"count(l) AS count\"))\n            .expect(\"Neo4j count query failed\");\n        id_from_i64(rows[0].get(\"count\").expect(\"count column\"))\n    }\n\n    fn create_links(\n        &mut self,\n        _query: &[T],\n        handler: WriteHandler<'_, T>,\n    ) -> Result<Flow,       flow\n    }\n\n    fn update_links(\n        &mut self,\n        query: &[T],\n        change: &[T],\n        handler: WriteHandler<'_, T>,\n    ) -> Result<Flow, Error<T>> {\n        let (id, source, target) = (query[0], change[1], change[2]);\n        let rows = self\n            .fetch_all(\n                neo4rs::query(\n                    \"MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) \\\n WriteHandler<'_, T>,\n    ) -> Result<Flow, Error<T>> {\n        let id = query[0];\n        let rows = self\n            .fetch_all(\n                neo4rs::query(\n                    \"MATCH     "stdout": "//! # Neo4j Implementation\n//!\n//! [`Neo4j`] implements the same [`Doublets`] interface as the Doublets stores,\n//! so every benchmark calls exactly the same methods on both databases.\n//!\n//! ## Driver and connection\n//!\n//! Neo4j is reached through [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs),\n//! the Bolt driver maintained by Neo4j Labs. Neo4j does not publish an\n//! official Rust driver.\n//!\n//! - The connection pool is opened once in [`Neo4j::connect`] and reused by\n//!   all operations, so no TCP connection is opened per operation.\n//! - All settings of the driver and of the server are defaults.\n//!\n//! ## Data model\n//!\n//! A link is a node with three integer properties:\n//!\n//! ```cypher\n//! (:Link {id: Integer, source: Integer, target: Integer})\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Links are found by the `id` property, which is backed by a uniqueness\n//! constraint (and therefore by an index). The internal node id (`elementId`)\n//! is not used, because Neo4j assigns it itself and may reuse it after a node\n//! is deleted, while a link id must be chosen by the caller and stay stable.\n//!\n//! ```cypher\n//! CREATE CONSTRAINT link_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) REQUIRE l.id IS UNIQUE\n//! CREATE INDEX link_source IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.source)\n//! CREATE INDEX link_target IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.target)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ## One statement per operation\n//!\n//! | Operation      | Cypher                                                                        |\n//! |----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | `create_point` | `CREATE (:Link {id: $id, source: $id, target: $id})`                          |\n//! | `update`       | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) WITH l, l.source AS source, l.target AS target SET l.source = $new_source, l.target = $new_target RETURN source, target` |\n//! | `delete`       | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) WITH l, l.source AS source, l.target AS target DELETE l RETURN source, target` |\n//! | `each_by`      | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN l.id AS id, l.source AS source, l.target AS target` |\n//! | `count_by`     | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN count(l) AS count`                 |\n//!\n//! `update` and `delete` return the previous `source` and `target` from the\n//! same statement, because the [`Doublets`] interface reports the link state\n//! before and after each change.\n//!\n//! New ids come from a counter kept by the client, as with a database\n//! sequence: `1, 2, 3, ...`. Doublets also assigns `1, 2, 3, ...` to the links\n//! of an empty store. As in Doublets, deleting the link with the highest id\n//! makes that id the next one to be created. Ids of other deleted links are not\n//! reused (Doublets reuses them too); the benchmarks only delete the links with\n//! the highest ids, so both databases always assign the same ids.\n//!\n//! ## Batches\n//!\n//! The `Neo4j_Batch` benchmarks send the parameters of all `N` operations of\n//! an iteration as one list, so the round trips, parsing and planning of a\n//! statement and the commit are paid once per list instead of once per link:\n//!\n//! | Method                | Cypher                                                                        |\n//! |-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | `create_points_batch` | `UNWIND range($first, $last) AS id CREATE (:Link {id: id, source: id, target: id})` |\n//! | `update_batch`        | `UNWIND $links AS link MATCH (l:Link {id: link[0]}) SET l.source = link[1], l.target = link[2] RETURN count(l) AS updated` |\n//! | `delete_batch`        | `UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l RETURN count(l) AS deleted` |\n//! | `each_by_batch`       | `UNWIND $queries AS q MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN ...`, `q` holds the constrained parts of one query |\n//!\n//! Neo4j finds every link of a list with the same index seek as the single\n//! statement does. The batch benchmarks use [`Mode::AutoCommit`], so every\n//! statement is one transaction. The Doublets interface has no batch methods,\n//! so these are methods of [`Neo4j`] only.\n//!\n//! ## Transaction modes\n//!\n//! | [`Mode`]                 | What happens                                                         |\n//! |--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | [`Mode::AutoCommit`]     | Every statement is its own transaction, committed by the server.     |\n//! | [`Mode::Transaction`]    | All statements between [`Neo4j::begin`] and [`Neo4j::commit`] run in one explicit transaction. |\n//!\n//! Errors returned by Neo4j are never ignored: methods that return `Result`\n//! return them as [`Error::Other`], and methods of the [`Links`] trait that\n//! cannot return an error (`each_links`, `count_links`) panic, which stops the\n//! benchmark.\n\nuse std::{\n    error,\n    sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard},\n};\n\nuse doublets::{\n    Doublets, Error, Link, Links,\n    data::{Flow, transactions.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Mode {\n    /// Every statement is a separate, automatically committed transaction.\n    AutoCommit,\n    /// Statements run in .iter()\n            .zip(query)\n            .filter(|&(_, &value)| value != self.constants.any)\n            .fold(\n                neo4rs::query(&format!(\"MATCH (l:Link){filter} RETURN The file size is measured after creation; Doublets files are\npreallocated memory-mapped files, so small stores show the preallocation size.\n\nEvery table is measured by its own GitHub Actions job, with all variants on\nthe same runner, so that a difference is never a difference between machines,\nby the [Benchmarks workflow](.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml): links with\n100,000, 1,000,000 and 10,000,000 records and objects with 100,000 and\n1,000,000 records. These are the largest sizes that fit into the 6 hour limit\nof a job: one SQLite File repetition on 100,000,000 links did not finish in\n4.5 hours\n([run 37228604862](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.SQLiteVSDoublets/actions/runs/37228604862)),\nand 1,000,000 blog posts already take an hour in C#. `(\"from\", \"to\")` and `(\"to\", \"from\")`; Doublets stores the links themselves.\n  The operations are create, read all, read by id, search by `(from, to)`,\n  read by `from`, read by `to`, update Every\n  Doublets store runs with and without a cache of the string sequences\n  (`Cached`/`Uncached`).\n\nStorages: SQLite in memory and in a file; Doublets united (one array of links\nwith index trees) and split (separate data and index arrays), each volatile\n(in memory) and non-volatile (in memory-mapped files). Doublets are compared\nwith SQLite of the same durability: volatile with `SQLite Memory`,\nnon-volatile with `SQLite File`.\n\nC# also runs `SystemDataSQLite_Memory` and `SystemDataSQLite_File` with\nSystem.Data.SQLite 2.0.4. `SQLite_Memory` and `SQLite_File` use\nMicrosoft.Data.Sqlite.         "content": "Docs\nLICENSE\nREADME.md\ndocs\nexperiments\nrust\nrust-toolchain.toml\n# Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets\n\nThis repository measures how long basic operations on links take in two\ndatabases:\n\n- **Neo4j** 2026.09 Community Edition with default settings, used from Rust\n  through the [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs) Bolt driver;\n- **Doublets**, the [doublets](https://crates.io/crates/doublets) Rust\n  library from LinksPlatform, used in the same process as the benchmark.\n\nA link (doublet) is a triple `(id, source, target)`. Both databases implement\nthe same [`Doublets`](https://docs.rs/doublets) interface, and every benchmark\ncalls the same methods on all of them.\n\nThe measured value is the time until an operation is finished from the point\nof view of the caller. Two workloads are reported:\n\n- **One operation per call**: every link operation is a separate call through\n  the `Doublets` interface, as an application calls it one at a time.\n- **Batch** (Neo4j only): the same operations of an iteration are sent to\n  Neo4j as one list in one Cypher statement, so the fixed cost of a statement\n  (round trips, query planning, commit) is paid once per iteration instead of\n  once per operation. Doublets has no batch calls; its batch work is the same\n  sequence of function calls as in the first workload.\n\n## What is compared\n\n| Implementation                | Where the data is                          | A finished operation is                            |\n|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `Doublets_United_Volatile`    | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n| `Doublets_United_NonVolatile` | memory-mapped file                         | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n| `Doublets_Split_Volatile`     | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n| `Doublets_Split_NonVolatile`  | two memory-mapped files                    | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n| `Neo4j_NonTransaction`        | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: every statement is its own transaction  |\n| `Neo4j_Transaction`           | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one explicit transaction per iteration  |\n| `Neo4j_Batch`                 | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one statement with all `N` operations   |\n\n- **United** and **Split** are two Doublets storage layouts: link data and\n  index trees in one array, or in two separate arrays.\n- Neo4j can only be reached over the network, so every Neo4j operation\n  includes at least one round trip to the server. Doublets has no server: its\n  operations are function calls on the process memory. The comparison\n  therefore shows the cost of each way of storing links as it is used, not the\n  cost of the storage engines alone.\n- Neo4j writes every commit to its transaction log on disk. The\n  [`neo4j`](https://crates.io/crates/neo4j) crate, which follows the API of the\n  official drivers, needs 2 and 1 because it sends several Bolt messages at\n  once ([`experiments`](experiments)). Neo4j does not publish an official Rust\n  driver.\n- **One client.** The benchmarks run operations one after another from one\n  thread. Throughput with concurrent clients is not measured.\n- **Only time is measured.** Memory use and disk I/O are not collected.\n- **Each Concrete** returns at most one link in Doublets, which treats a\n  `(source, target)` pair as unique; the benchmarks never create two links\n  with the same pair.\n- **At most 1,040,383 links.** The doublets 0.5.0 stores panic when link\n  number 1,040,384 is created: after growing their memory, they use only the\n  newly added part of it as the whole array (see\n  [`experiments/store-capacity`](experiments/store-capacity) and the\n  \"Capacity\" section of [`rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`](rust/src/doublets_impl.rs)).\n  This is why `B` stops at 1,000,000.\n- **Point links only.** The doublets 0.5.0 Split store does not find links\n  with `source != target` by `[*, source, *]` and `[*, source, target]` queries\n  after an `update` (see\n  [`experiments/split-store-bug`](experiments/split-store-bug)). The\n  benchmarks only use point links and links updated to `(0, 0)` and back, for\n  which all stores return the same results.\n- Results before [issue #15](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/issues/15)\n  were measured with an HTTP client that opened a new connection for every\n  request and are not comparable with the current results.\n\n## Running locally\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name neo4j -p 7687:7687 -e NEO4J_AUTH=neo…ord neo4j:2026.09-community\n\ncd rust\ncargo test --release -- --include-ignored     # Details below |\n| `pipeline-status` | — | Gate job: checks the final status of all needed jobs |\n\n`publish_benchmarks.py`:\n- works in a git worktree\n- retries a lost push race 3 times\n- **refuses to publish if the source changed since the measured SHA**\n- commits `Update benchmark results [skip ci]`\n\n**`rust.yml` and `csharp.yml`**\n- Path filtered, workflow concurrency with cancel-in-progress, timeout 30.\n- OS matrix: ubuntu-24.04, macos-15, windows-2025.\n- Rust steps:\n  - `cargo fmt --check`, including experiments\n  - `cargo clippy --locked --release --all-targets -- -D warnings`\n  - `cargo test --locked --release`\n- C# steps:\n  - `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes`\n  - `build -warnaserror`\n  - tests with `--timeout 10m`\n  - a PostgreSQL integration job\n\n**`quality.yml`**\n- Runs:\n  - actionlint and ShellCheck in a container pinned by digest\n  - zizmor at two strictness levels\n  - ruff check, ruff format, mypy and bandit\n  - `ci_checks.py` and the unittests\n  - markdownlint and secretlint\n  - the `pipeline-status` gate\n- All actions are pinned by SHA and runner images are pinned (no `-latest`).\n\n**`ci_checks.py` enforces:**\n- every job has a timeout\n- no `latest` runners\n- no `continue-on-error`\n- the publishing job is serialized\n- source files are at most 1500 lines\n- the required README sections and markers exist\n- local links are valid\n\n### Tests\n- `rust/tests/storages.rs` and `StoragesTests.cs` are confirmed to contain:\n  - `every_links_variant_passes_the_lifecycle`\n  - `every_objects_variant_passes_the_lifecycle`\n  - `lifecycle_rejects_a_storage_that_loses_records` (a deliberately lossy storage that must fail)\n  - `stores_keep_their_links_when_their_memory_grows`\n  - `split_store_keeps_links_updated_to_reference_themselves`\n  - `every_objects_storage_returns_the_stored_posts`\n  - dataset uniqueness and scatter tests\n- Every backend is checked against the same expected count and checksum. That is in effect a test that all implementations agree.\n\n### Practices worth copying\n- The ratio rule: IQR overlap or a gap under 5% gives \"≈ same\", and both \"faster\" and \"slower\" are shown.\n- Formatting to 3 significant digits with automatic ns/µs/ms/s units.\n- Provenance line: repetitions, library version, machine, a link to the run, and the date.\n- Raw JSON is committed with the results.\n- Data is validated (count and checksum) before any timing is trusted.\n- A lossy-storage test proves the validation actually works.\n- Separate PR and main sizes; a separate job per language, category, bits and size.\n- A single serialized writer with push retry and a check that the measured SHA is still current; `[skip ci]` in the commit.\n- On PRs the README is regenerated and linted without committing.\n- `ci_checks.py` statically enforces CI rules (timeouts, pinned runners, README sections).\n- A bilingual README, and CONTRIBUTING with the exact local commands.\n\n### Issues and PRs\n- **All issues are closed:** #110, #107, #105, #103, #101, #42, #33, #29, #28, #15, #6, #3, #1.\n  - #110: CI false positives and negatives\n  - #107: clearly divide benchmark categories and cover them evenly\n  - #105: Rust doublets with a Rust SQLite client\n  - #103: Rust-only benchmark using best practices\n  - #101: move C# into `./csharp`\n  - #33: Npgsql EF Core\n  - #6: BenchmarkDotNet\n- **Relevant merged PRs:**\n  - #111: Truthful CI checks and hardened publication\n  - #108: Symmetric Rust/C# by category, language, bits and size\n  - #100: System.Data.SQLite\n  - #99: EF Core PostgreSQL\n  - also #112, #109, #106, #104, #102, #98\n  - many Dependabot bumps from #2 to #97\n\n### What it lacks compared with the others and Neo4j\n- No linear chart and no 0.5% minimum bar width (log only).\n- No section called \"Limitations\" (the \"Notes\" section partly covers it).\n- No formal table of environment variables (`POSTGRESQL_CONNECTION_STRING` and `POSTGRESQL_VERBOSE` are only mentioned in prose).\n- The Conclusion is hand-written and stale, not generated.\n- Criterion is not used, which is acceptable because the custom harness is deliberate.\n\n---\n\n## 2. `BASELINE = \"SpacetimeDB\"`)\n```python\ndef format_speedup(value, baseline):\n    \"\"\"Annotate ``value`` with how it compares to the ``baseline`` measurement.\"\"\"\n    if not value:\n        return \"N/A\"\n    if not baseline:\n        return f\"{value}\"\n    if value <= baseline:\n        return f\"{value} ({baseline / value:.1f}x faster)\"\n    return f\"{value} ({value / baseline:.1f}x slower)\"\n```\n- The baseline column shows the raw value.\n- Provenance, lines 165-188:\n  `f\"_Generated {generated_at} by {source} — {benchmark_links} benchmarked links, {background_links} background links._\"`\n  where `source` links to the Actions run.\n\n### README results excerpt\n```\n| Create | 76689 (33385.0x faster) | 76567 (33438.2x faster) | 47102 (54355.7x faster) | 47395 (54019.7x faster) | 2560262853 |\n| Query All | 21580 (1.0x faster) | 21592 (1.0x faster) | 28388 (1.3x slower) | 28312 (1.3x slower) | 22126 |\n```\n- The text under the table says: \"Each Doublets cell is annotated with how many times faster (or slower) it is than SpacetimeDB for the same operation.\"\n- **README sections:**\n  - Benchmark Operations table\n  - Backends Benchmarked\n  - Benchmark Background: env vars `BACKGROUND_LINK_COUNT` (default 3000) and `BENCHMARK_LINK_COUNT` (default 1000), as bullets\n  - Results: linear and log images\n  - the marker section\n  - Conclusion: an architectural explanation\n  - Operation Complexity table\n  - Related Benchmarks\n  - Running Benchmarks: prerequisites, server, run, tests, code quality\n  - Project Structure\n  - License\n\n### Charts (`_plot`, lines 236-273)\n- Horizontal grouped bars, width 0.15, `figsize=(12,8)`.\n- Colors: salmon, red, lightgreen and green for the Doublets variants; After every\n/// iteration `undo` puts the store back into the same state, so every\n/// iteration starts from the same links. Neither of them is measured.\npub(crate) fn measure<B: Benched>(\n    group: &mut BenchmarkGroup<WallTime>,\n    id: &str,\n    benched: &mut B,\n    mut operation: impl FnMut(&mut B) -> Result<()>,\n    mut undo: impl FnMut(&mut B) -> Result<()>,\n) {\n    let mut benched = Some(benched);\n    let mut store = None;\n    let mut iteration = |store: &mut B| -> Result<Duration> {\n        let started store.commit()?;\n        Ok(elapsed)\n    };\n    group.bench_function(id, |bencher| {\n        let store = store.get_or_insert_with(|| {\n            let benched = benched.take().expect(\"the store bencher.iter_custom(|iterations| {\n            (0..iterations)\n                .map(|_| iteration(store).expect(\"benchmark iteration failed\"))\n                .sum()\n        })\n    });\n}\n\n/// Nothing to undo.\npub(crate) fn read_only<B>(_: &mut B) -> Result<()> {\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Consumes every found link, so the compiler cannot skip reading it.\npub(crate) fn benched, |id| [any, any, id]);\n}\n//! # Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets\n//!\n//! This crate measures how long basic link operations take when the links are\n//! stored in Neo4j and when they are stored in Doublets.\n//!\n//! Both databases implement the same [`Doublets`](doublets::Doublets) trait,\n//! and every benchmark calls the same trait methods on every backend:\n//!\n//! - **[`neo4j_impl`]** - how Neo4j implements each operation (Cypher via the\n//!   neo4rs Bolt driver)\n//! - **[`doublets_impl`]** - how Doublets implements each operation (direct\n//!   access to its in-process data structures)\n//!\n//! ## Operations\n//!\n//! | Operation       | Method                  | Description                                    |\n//! | `Doublets_United_NonVolatile` | in-process, memory-mapped file   | in the OS page cache, no `fsync`          |\n//! | `Doublets_Split_Volatile`     | in-process, RAM, split store     | none (RAM only)                           |\n//! | `Doublets_Split_NonVolatile`  | in-process, memory-mapped files  | in the OS page cache, no `fsync`          |\n//! | `Neo4j_NonTransaction`        | Neo4j server over Bolt           | committed (auto-commit per statement)     |\n//! | `Neo4j_Transaction`           | Neo4j server over Bolt           | committed once per iteration              |\n//! | `Neo4j_Batch`                 | Neo4j server over Bolt           | one statement with all `N` operations     |\n//!\n//! ## How the Benchmark Works\n//!\n//! For every operation and store:\n//! 1. [`Benched::fork`] creates [`background_links`] point links (not measured)\n//! 2. every iteration runs the operation [`benchmark_links`] times between\n//!                 "-            if not line.startswith(\"test \"):",
                "-                continue",
                "-            # A line without a time means the benchmark reported an error",
                "-            # instead of its result; such a run must not be published.",

                "-            if not match:",
                "-                raise SystemExit(f\"{path}: no result in line: {line}\")",

                "-            operation = group.replace(\"_\", \" \")",
                "-            times[(operation, implementation)] = int(ns.replace(\",\", \"\"))",

                "-            f\"| {operation} | \" + \" | \".join(f\"{cell:,}\" if cell else \"N/A\" for cell in cells) + \" |\"",

                "-        offset = (index - (len(IMPLEMENTATIONS) - 1) / 2) * width",

                "-        ax.set_xscale(\"log\")",

                "-    ax.legend(loc=\"upper left\", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1))",

                "-    fig.savefig(path)",

      "content": "//! # Neo4j Implementation\n//!\n//! [`Neo4j`] implements the same [`Doublets`] interface as the Doublets stores,\n//! so every benchmark calls exactly the same methods on both databases.\n//!\n//! ## Driver and connection\n//!\n//! Neo4j is reached through [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs),\n//! the Bolt driver maintained by Neo4j Labs. Neo4j does not publish an\n//! official Rust driver.\n//!\n//! - The connection pool is opened once in [`Neo4j::connect`] and reused by\n//!   all operations, so no TCP connection is opened per operation.\n//! - All settings of the driver and of the server are defaults.\n//!\n//! ## Data model\n//!\n//! A link is a node with three integer properties:\n//!\n//! ```cypher\n//! (:Link {id: Integer, source: Integer, target: Integer})\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Links are found by the `id` property, which is backed by a uniqueness\n//! constraint (and therefore by an index). The internal node id (`elementId`)\n//! is not used, because Neo4j assigns it itself and may reuse it after a node\n//! is deleted, while a link id must be chosen by the caller and stay stable.\n//!\n//! ```cypher\n//! CREATE CONSTRAINT link_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) REQUIRE l.id IS UNIQUE\n//! CREATE INDEX link_source IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.source)\n//! CREATE INDEX link_target IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.target)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ## One statement per operation\n//!\n//! | Operation      | Cypher                                                                        |\n//! |----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | `create_point` | `CREATE (:Link {id: $id, source: $id, target: $id})`                          |\n//! | `update`       | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) WITH l, l.source AS source, l.target AS target SET l.source = $new_source, l.target = $new_target RETURN source, target` |\n//! | `delete`       | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) WITH l, l.source AS source, l.target AS target DELETE l RETURN source, target` |\n//! | `each_by`      | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN l.id AS id, l.source AS source, l.target AS target` |\n//! | `count_by`     | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN count(l) AS count`                 |\n//!\n//! `update` and `delete` return the previous `source` and `target` from the\n//! same statement, because the [`Doublets`] interface reports the link state\n//! before and after each change.\n//!\n//! New ids come from a counter kept by the client, as with a database\n//! sequence: `1, 2, 3, ...`. Doublets also assigns `1, 2, 3, ...` to the links\n//! of an empty store. As in Doublets, deleting the link with the highest id\n//! makes that id the next one to be created. Ids of other deleted links are not\n//! reused (Doublets reuses them too); the benchmarks only delete the links with\n//! the highest ids, so both databases always assign the same ids.\n//!\n//! ## Batches\n//!\n//! The `Neo4j_Batch` benchmarks send the parameters of all `N` operations of\n//! an iteration as one list, so the round trips, parsing and planning of a\n//! statement and the commit are paid once per list instead of once per link:\n//!\n//! | Method                | Cypher                                                                        |\n//! |-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | `create_points_batch` | `UNWIND range($first, $last) AS id CREATE (:Link {id: id, source: id, target: id})` |\n//! | `update_batch`        | `UNWIND $links AS link MATCH (l:Link {id: link[0]}) SET l.source = link[1], l.target = link[2] RETURN count(l) AS updated` |\n//! | `delete_batch`        | `UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l RETURN count(l) AS deleted` |\n//! | `each_by_batch`       | `UNWIND $queries AS q MATCH (l:Link) WHERE <constraints> RETURN ...`, `q` holds the constrained parts of one query |\n//!\n//! Neo4j finds every link of a list with the same index seek as the single\n//! statement does. The batch benchmarks use [`Mode::AutoCommit`], so every\n//! statement is one transaction. The Doublets interface has no batch methods,\n//! so these are methods of [`Neo4j`] only.\n//!\n//! ## Transaction modes\n//!\n//! | [`Mode`]                 | What happens                                                         |\n//! |--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n//! | [`Mode::AutoCommit`]     | Every statement is its own transaction, committed by the server.     |\n//! | [`Mode::Transaction`]    | All statements between [`Neo4j::begin`] and [`Neo4j::commit`] run in one explicit transaction. |\n//!\n//! Errors returned by Neo4j are never ignored: methods that return `Result`\n//! return them as [`Error::Other`], and methods of the [`Links`] trait that\n//! cannot return an error (`each_links`, `count_links`) panic, which stops the\n//! benchmark.\n\nuse std::{\n    error,\n    sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard},\n};\n\nuse doublets::{\n    Doublets, Error, Link, Links,\n    data::{Flow, LinkReference, LinksConstants, ReadHandler, WriteHandler},\n};\nuse neo4rs::{Graph, Query, Row, Txn, query};\nuse tokio::runtime::Runtime;\n\n/// How statements are grouped into transactions.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Mode {\n    /// Every statement is a separate, automatically committed transaction.\n    AutoCommit,\n    /// Statements run in one explicit transaction until [`Neo4j::commit`].\n    Transaction,\n}\n\n/// A links store kept in a Neo4j database.\npub struct Neo4j<T: LinkReference> {\n    /// Runs the asynchronous driver calls to completion on the calling thread.\n    runtime: Runtime,\n    graph: Graph,\n    mode: Mode,\n    /// The open explicit transaction, used only in [`Mode::Transaction`].\n    transaction: Mutex<Option<Txn>>,\n    constants: LinksConstants<T>,\n    next_id: T,\n}\n\n/// Number of links created or deleted per transaction by\n/// [`Neo4j::create_points`] and [`Neo4j::clear`].\npub const BATCH_SIZE: usize = 10_000;\n\n/// Result of a driver call.\ntype Neo4jResult<T> = Result<T, neo4rs::Error>;\n\nimpl<T: LinkReference> Neo4j<T> {\n    /// Opens the connection pool and creates the schema if it does not exist.\n    pub fn connect(uri: &str, user: &str, password: &str, mode: Mode) -> crate::Result<Self> {\n        let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()\n            .enable_all()\n            .build()?;\n        let graph = runtime.block_on(Graph::new(uri, user, password))?;\n        let store = Self {\n            runtime,\n            graph,\n            mode,\n            transaction: Mutex::new(None),\n            constants: LinksConstants::new(),\n            next_id: T::from_byte(1),\n        };\n        for statement in [\n            \"CREATE CONSTRAINT link_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) REQUIRE l.id IS UNIQUE\",\n            \"CREATE INDEX link_source IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.source)\",\n            \"CREATE INDEX link_target IF NOT EXISTS FOR (l:Link) ON (l.target)\",\n        ] {\n            store.run_auto_commit(query(statement))?;\n        }\n        store.run_auto_commit(query(\"CALL db.awaitIndexes()\"))?;\n        Ok(store)\n    }\n\n    /// Opens the connection described by the `NEO4J_URI`, `NEO4J_USER` and\n    /// `NEO4J_PASSWORD` environment variables (defaults:\n    /// `bolt://localhost:7687`, `neo4j`, Self::connect(\n            &var(\"NEO4J_URI\", \"bolt://localhost:7687\"),\n            &var(\"NEO4J_USER\", \"neo4j\"),\n            &var(\"NEO4J_PASSWORD\", \"password\"),\n            mode,\n        )\n    }\n\n    pub fn mode(&self) -> Mode {\n        self.mode\n    }\n\n    /// Creates `count` point links with the next ids, committing every\n    /// [`BATCH_SIZE`] links, so that millions of links do not have to fit into\n    /// the memory of one transaction.\n    ///\n    /// Used to prepare the background links outside of the measured time.\n    pub fn create_points(&mut self, count: \"UNWIND range($first, $last) AS id \\\n                 CALL (id) {{ CREATE (:Link {{id: id, source: id, target: id}}) }} \\\n                 IN TRANSACTIONS OF {BATCH_SIZE} ROWS\"\n            ))\n
