when the store is in [`Mode::Transaction`].\n    pub fn begin(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        if self.mode == Mode::Transaction {\n            let transaction = self.runtime.block_on(self.graph.start_txn())?;\n            *self.transaction() = Some(transaction);\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Commits the explicit transaction started by [`Neo4j::begin`], if any.\n    pub fn commit(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        if let Some(transaction) = self.transaction().take() {\n            self.runtime.block_on(transaction.commit())?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rolls back the open transaction, if any, and deletes all links,\n    /// committing every [`BATCH_SIZE`] links.\n    pub fn clear(&mut self) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        if let Some(transaction) = self.transaction().take() {\n            self.runtime.block_on(transaction.rollback())?;\n        }\n        self.run_auto_commit(query(&format!(\n            \"MATCH (l:Link) CALL (l) {{ DELETE l }} IN TRANSACTIONS OF {BATCH_SIZE} ROWS\"\n        )))?;\n        self.next_id = T::from_byte(1);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn transaction(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Option<Txn>> {\n        self.transaction\n            .lock()\n            .expect(\"transaction mutex is poisoned\")\n    }\n\n    fn run_auto_commit(&self, query: Query) -> Neo4jResult<()> {\n        self.runtime.block_on(self.graph.run(query))\n    }\n\n    /// Runs `query` in the open transaction (or as an auto-commit\n    /// transaction) and passes every returned row to `on_row`.\n    // The lock is held only by this thread while `block_on` runs the query on\n    // the store's own single-threaded runtime, so no other task can wait for it.\n    #[allow(clippy::await_holding_lock)]\n    fn fetch(&self, query: Query, mut on_row: impl FnMut(Row)) -> Neo4jResult<()> {\n        self.runtime.block_on(async {\n            match self.transaction().as_mut() {\n                Some(transaction) => {\n                    let mut rows = transaction.execute(query).await?;\n                    while let Some(row) = rows.next(transaction.handle()).await? {\n                        on_row(row);\n                    }\n                }\n                None => {\n                    let mut rows = self.graph.execute(query).await?;\n                    while let Some(row) = rows.next().await? {\n                        on_row(row);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(())\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Runs `query` and returns its rows.\n    fn fetch_all(&self, query: Query) -> Neo4jResult<Vec<Row>> {\n        let mut rows = Vec::new();\n        self.fetch(query, |row| rows.push(row))?;\n        Ok(rows)\n    }\n\n    /// Builds `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE ...` for a doublets query\n    /// (`[]`, `[id]` or `[id, source, target]`, where `any` matches everything).\n    fn match_query(&self, query: &[T], returns: &str) -> Query {\n        let filter = self.filter(query, |part| format!(\"${}\", PARTS[part]));\n        PARTS\n            .iter()\n            .zip(query)\n            .filter(|&(_, &value)| value != self.constants.any)\n            .fold(\n                neo4rs::query(&format!(\"MATCH (l:Link){filter} RETURN {returns}\")),\n                |q, (name, &value)| q.param(name, id_to_i64(value)),\n            )\n    }\n\n    /// Builds the ` WHERE ...` clause with one condition per part of `query`\n    /// that is not `any`; `value(part)` is the Cypher expression the property\n    /// is compared with.\n    fn filter(&self, query: &[T], value: impl Fn(usize) -> String) -> String {\n        let conditions: Vec<_> = PARTS\n            .iter()\n            .zip(query)\n            .enumerate()\n            .filter(|&(_, (_, &part))| part != self.constants.any)\n            .map(|(part, (name, _))| format!(\"l.{name} = {}\", value(part)))\n            .collect();\n        if conditions.is_empty() {\n            String::new()\n        } else {\n            format!(\" WHERE {}\", conditions.join(\" AND \"))\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Batches: one statement for many links (the `Neo4j_Batch` benchmarks)\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Creates the point links with the next `count` ids with one statement.\n    pub fn create_points_batch(&mut self, count: usize) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let first = id_to_i64(self.next_id);\n        let last = first + count as i64 - 1;\n        self.fetch_all(\n            query(\n                \"UNWIND range($first, $last) AS id \\\n                 CREATE (:Link {id: id, source: id, target: id})\",\n            )\n            .param(\"first\", first)\n            .param(\"last\", last),\n        )?;\n        self.next_id = id_from_i64(last + 1);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Sets `source` and `target` of every link in `links` (found by its\n    /// `index`) with one statement.\n    pub fn update_batch(&mut self, links: &[Link<T>]) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let expected = links.len();\n        let links: Vec<_> = links\n            .iter()\n            .map(|link| {\n                [link.index, link.source, link.target]\n                    .map(id_to_i64)\n                    .to_vec()\n            })\n            .collect();\n        let rows = self.fetch_all(\n            query(\n                \"UNWIND $links AS link \\\n                 MATCH (l:Link {id: link[0]}) \\\n                 SET l.source = link[1], l.target = link[2] \\\n                 RETURN count(l) AS updated\",\n            )\n            .param(\"links\", links),\n        )?;\n        expect_count(&rows, \"updated\", expected)\n    }\n\n    /// Deletes the links with the given ids with one statement.\n    pub fn delete_batch(&mut self, ids: &[T]) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let rows = self.fetch_all(\n            query(\n                \"UNWIND $ids AS id \\\n                 MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) \\\n                 DELETE l \\\n                 RETURN count(l) AS deleted\",\n            )\n            .param(\n                \"ids\",\n                ids.iter().copied().map(id_to_i64).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n            ),\n        )?;\n        expect_count(&rows, \"deleted\", ids.len())?;\n        // The same rule as in `delete_links`, applied from the highest id.\n        let mut ids = ids.to_vec();\n        ids.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.cmp(a));\n        for id in ids {\n            if id + T::from_byte(1) == self.next_id {\n                self.next_id = id;\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Runs all `queries` with one statement and passes every found link to\n    /// `handler`.\n    ///\n    /// All queries must constrain the same parts (for example, all are\n    /// `[*, source, *]`), because they share one `WHERE` clause.\n    pub fn each_by_batch(\n        &self,\n        queries: &[[T; 3]],\n        mut handler: impl FnMut(Link<T>),\n    ) -> crate::Result<()> {\n        let Some(first) = queries.first() else {\n            return Ok(());\n |-----------------|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------|\n//! | Create          | `create_point()`        | Insert a point link (id = source = target)     |\n//! This module documents how the [doublets](https://crates.io/crates/doublets)\n//! stores implement the [`Doublets`](doublets::Doublets) interface. The stores\n//! run inside the benchmark process: every operation reads and writes the\n//! store's memory directly, without a server, a network connection or a query\n//! language.\n//!\n//! ## Stores\n//!\n//! A link is identified by its position in an array: link `id` is element\n//! `id` of the array. Two size-balanced trees index the links, one ordered by\n//! `(source, target)` and one ordered by `(target, source)`. The tree nodes\n//! are stored in the array elements as well, so no memory is allocated per\n//! link.\n//!\n//! ### United (unit) store\n//!\n//! One array; each element holds the link and its nodes of both trees:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! Two arrays: the link data and the tree nodes are kept apart, so reading\n//! links does not load tree nodes into the CPU cache:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! DataPart:  source, target\n//! IndexPart: root_as_source, left_as_source, right_as_source, size_as_source,\n//!            root_as_target, left_as_target, right_as_target, size_as_target\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ```\n//! use doublets::{mem::Global, split, Doublets};\n//!\n//! let mut store = split::Store::<usize, _, _>::new(Global::new(), Global::new())?;\n//! let id = store.create_point()?;\n//! assert_eq!(store.get_link(id).map(|link| (link.source, link.target)), Some((id, id)));\n//! # Ok::<(), doublets::Error<usize>>(())\n//! ```\n//!\n//! ### Volatile and non-volatile\n//!\n//! The benchmarks never create two links\n//! with the same pair.\n//!\n//! ## Capacity\n//!\n//! The doublets 0.5.0 stores hold at most [`MAX_LINKS`] links. A store\n//! reserves space for `2^20` array elements in steps: first `8192`, then the\n//! rest. `platform-mem` 0.3.0 returns only the newly added part of the memory\n//! from the second step, and the store uses that part as the whole array, so\n//! `8192` elements are missing and creating link number `2^20 - 8192`\n//! panics (\"Data part should be in data memory\" in the united store, \"Index\n//! part should be in index memory\" in the split store) instead of growing the\n//! array (see `experiments/store-capacity`). A link is identified by its position in an array: link `id` is element\n//! `id` of the array. The values are the ones of the Rust benchmarks (<c>rust/benches/benchmarks/mod.rs</c>),\n/// and the iteration counts are chosen as Criterion 0.8 chooses them, so both languages measure the same way.\n/// </summary>\n/// <param name=\"SampleSize\">Number of samples.</param>\n/// <param name=\"Flat\">Every sample has the same number of iterations (Criterion's flat sampling);\n/// otherwise sample <c>i</c> has <c>i × d</c> iterations (linear sampling).</param>\n/// <param name=\"WarmUp\">How long the benchmark runs before it is measured.</param>\n/// <param name=\"MeasurementTime\">The measured time that all samples take together.</param>\npublic sealed record Sampling(int SampleSize, bool Flat, TimeSpan WarmUp, TimeSpan MeasurementTime)\n{\n    /// <summary>One Neo4j iteration takes milliseconds, so 10 samples of the same number of iterations already give stable results.</summary>\n    public static Sampling Neo4j { get; } = new(10, true, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));\n\n    /// <summary>One Doublets iteration takes microseconds, so 100 samples are used to measure it precisely.</summary>\n    public static Sampling Doublets { get; } = new(100, false, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2));\n\n    /// <summary>The number of iterations of every sample, for iterations that take <paramref name=\"nanoseconds\"/> each.</summary>\n    public long[] IterationCounts(double nanoseconds)\n    {\n        var measurement = MeasurementTime.TotalNanoseconds;\n        if (Flat)\n        {\n            var iterations = Math.Max(1, (long)Math.Ceiling(measurement / (nanoseconds * SampleSize)));\n            return Enumerable.Repeat(iterations, SampleSize).ToArray();\n        }\n        var totalRuns = (double)SampleSize * (SampleSize + 1) / 2;\n        var step = Math.Max(1, (long)Math.Ceiling(measurement / nanoseconds / totalRuns));\n        return Enumerable.Range(1, SampleSize).Select(sample => sample * step).ToArray();\n    }\n}\n\n/// <summary>The median time of one iteration and the standard deviation of the samples, in nanoseconds.</summary>\npublic readonly record struct Estimate(double Median, double StandardDeviation)\n{\n    /// <summary>Estimates the time of one iteration from the average iteration time of every sample.</summary>\n    public static Estimate Of(IReadOnlyCollection<double> samples)\n    {\n        var sorted = samples.Order().ToArray();\n        var middle = sorted.Length / 2;\n        var median = sorted.Length % 2 == 0 ? (sorted[middle - 1] + sorted[middle]) / 2 : sorted[middle];\n        var mean = sorted.Average();\n        var variance = sorted.Length > 1 ? sorted.Sum(sample => (sample - mean) * (sample - mean)) / (sorted.Length - 1) : 0;\n        return new Estimate(median, Math.Sqrt(variance));\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// The line that Criterion prints with <c>--output-format bencher</c>, for example\n    /// <c>test Create/Neo4j_Transaction ... bench:  44,055,505 ns/iter (+/- 5,345,991)</c>.\n    /// </summary>\n    public string Bencher(string group, string id) =>\n        string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,\n            $\"test {group}/{id} ... bench: {Math.Round(Median),11:N0} ns/iter (+/- {Math.Round(StandardDeviation):N0})\");\n}\n\npublic static class Harness\n{\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Measures <paramref name=\"iteration\"/>, which runs one iteration and returns its measured time:\n    /// first warms up for <see cref=\"Sampling.WarmUp\"/>, doubling the number of iterations each round,\n    /// then takes <see cref=\"Sampling.SampleSize\"/> samples.\n    /// </summary>\n    public static Estimate Measure(Sampling sampling, Func<TimeSpan> iteration)\n    {\n        TimeSpan Run(long iterations)\n        {\n            var elapsed = TimeSpan.Zero;\n            for (long i = 0; i < iterations; i++)\n            {\n                elapsed += iteration();\n            }\n            return elapsed;\n        }\n\n        var warmUp = TimeSpan.Zero;\n        long warmUpIterations = 0;\n        for (long iterations = 1; warmUp < sampling.WarmUp; iterations *= 2)\n        {\n            warmUp += Run(iterations);\n            warmUpIterations += iterations;\n        }\n        var counts = sampling.IterationCounts(Math.Max(1, warmUp.TotalNanoseconds / warmUpIterations));\n        return Estimate.Of(counts.Select(count => Run(count).TotalNanoseconds / count).ToArray());\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Measures <paramref name=\"operation\"/> on <paramref name=\"store\"/>, which contains <see cref=\"Settings.BackgroundLinks\"/>\n    /// point links. After every iteration <paramref name=\"undo\"/> puts the store back into the same state, so every\n    /// iteration starts from the same links. Neither the background links nor the undo are measured.\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <remarks>\n    /// The measured time starts before <see cref=\"IBenchedLinks.Begin\"/> and ends after <see cref=\"IBenchedLinks.Commit\"/>,\n    /// so for Neo4j in transaction mode it includes starting and committing the transaction.\n    /// </remarks>\n    public static Estimate Measure<TStore>(Sampling sampling, TStore store, Action<TStore> operation, Action<TStore> undo)\n        where TStore : IBenchedLinks\n    {\n        store.Fork(Settings.BackgroundLinks);\n        try\n        {\n            return Measure(sampling, () =>\n            {\n                var started = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();\n                store.Begin();\n                operation(store);\n                store.Commit();\n                var elapsed = Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime(started);\n\n                store.Begin();\n                undo(store);\n                store.Commit();\n                return elapsed;\n            });\n        }\n        finally\n        {\n            store.Unfork();\n        }\n    }\n}\n"

}`\n         - `void Fork(int backgroundLinks)` and `void Unfork()`\n         - `void Begin() {}` and `void Commit() {}` (default no-ops)\n         - `ulong CreatePoint()`, `void Update(ulong id, ulong source, ulong target)` and `void Delete(ulong id)`\n         - `void Each(ulong id, ulong source, ulong target, Action<Link> visit)` and `ulong Count()`\n     - **Settings.cs:**\n       - `BackgroundLinks` reads BENCHMARK_BACKGROUND_LINKS (default 1000).\n       - `BenchmarkLinks` reads BENCHMARK_LINKS (default 100) and throws if it exceeds BackgroundLinks.\n       - `Backend` reads BENCHMARK_BACKEND.\n       - `Variable(name, fallback)` returns an environment variable or the fallback.\n       - `Number` throws on a value that is not a non-negative integer.\n     - **DoubletsLinks.cs:** `public sealed class DoubletsLinks(ILinks<ulong> links) : IBenchedLinks`.\n       - `static string[] Variants` lists the four store names.\n       - `Open(variant, directory)`:\n         - Uses `UnitedMemoryLinks<ulong>` or `SplitMemoryLinks<ulong>`.\n         - Memory is `HeapResizableDirectMemory` for the volatile stores.\n         - The non-volatile stores use `FileMappedResizableDirectMemory` on united.links, split_data.links and split_index.links.         "content": "1:# Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets\n2:\n3:This repository measures how long basic operations on links take in two\n4:databases:\n5:\n6:- **Neo4j** 2026.09 Community Edition with default settings, used from Rust\n7:  through the [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs) Bolt driver;\n8:- **Doublets**, the [doublets](https://crates.io/crates/doublets) Rust\n9:  library from LinksPlatform, used in the same process as the benchmark.\n10:\n11:A link (doublet) is a triple `(id, source, target)`. Both databases implement\n12:the same [`Doublets`](https://docs.rs/doublets) interface, and every benchmark\n13:calls the same methods on all of them.\n14:\n15:The measured value is the time until an operation is finished from the point\n16:of view of the caller. Two workloads are reported:\n17:\n18:- **One operation per call**: every link operation is a separate call through\n19:  the `Doublets` interface, as an application calls it one at a time.\n20:- **Batch** (Neo4j only): the same operations of an iteration are sent to\n21:  Neo4j as one list in one Cypher statement, so the fixed cost of a statement\n22:  (round trips, query planning, commit) is paid once per iteration instead of\n23:  once per operation. Doublets has no batch calls; its batch work is the same\n24:  sequence of function calls as in the first workload.\n25:\n26:## What is compared\n27:\n28:| Implementation                | Where the data is                          | A finished operation is                            |\n29:|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n30:| `Doublets_United_Volatile`    | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n31:| `Doublets_United_NonVolatile` | memory-mapped file                         | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n32:| `Doublets_Split_Volatile`     | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n33:| `Doublets_Split_NonVolatile`  | two memory-mapped files                    | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n34:| `Neo4j_NonTransaction`        | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: every statement is its own transaction  |\n35:| `Neo4j_Transaction`           | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one explicit transaction per iteration  |\n36:| `Neo4j_Batch`                 | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one statement with all `N` operations   |\n37:\n38:- **United** and **Split** are two Doublets storage layouts: link data and\n39:  index trees in one array, or in two separate arrays.\n40:- Neo4j can only be reached over the network, so every Neo4j operation\n41:  includes at least one round trip to the server. Doublets has no server: its\n42:  operations are function calls on the process memory. The comparison\n43:  therefore shows the cost of each way of storing links as it is used, not the\n44:  cost of the storage engines alone.\n45:- Neo4j writes every commit to its transaction log on disk. The Doublets stores\n46:  do not call `fsync`.\n47:\n48:## Operations\n49:\n50:| Operation     | `Doublets` method            | Neo4j (Cypher, one statement)                              | Doublets                                     |\n51:|---------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|\n52:| Create        | `create_point()`             | `CREATE (:Link {id: $id, source: $id, target: $id})`       | write the link, insert it into both trees    |\n53:| Update        | `update(id, source, target)` | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) ... SET l.source = ..., l.target = ...` | remove from both trees, write, insert  |\n54:| Delete        | `delete(id)`                 | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) ... DELETE l`                    | remove from both trees, mark as free         |\n55:| Each All      | `each([*, *, *])`            | `MATCH (l:Link) RETURN ...`                                | scan the array                               |\n56:| Each Identity | `each_by([id, *, *])`        | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.id = $id RETURN ...`               | read array element `id`                      |\n57:| Each Concrete | `each_by([*, source, target])` | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.source = $source AND l.target = $target RETURN ...` | search the `(source, target)` tree |\n58:| Each Outgoing | `each_by([*, source, *])`    | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.source = $source RETURN ...`       | walk the `(source, target)` tree             |\n59:| Each Incoming | `each_by([*, *, target])`    | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.target = $target RETURN ...`       | walk the `(target, source)` tree             |\n60:\n61:In Neo4j a link is a node `(:Link {id, source, target})`. A link is found by\n62:its `id` property, which has a uniqueness constraint and therefore an index;\n63:`source` and `target` have indexes too. The internal node id (`elementId`) is\n64:not used as the link id, because Neo4j chooses it itself and may reuse it,\n65:while link ids are chosen by the caller. Update and Delete are single\n66:statements that also return the previous `source` and `target`, which the\n67:`Doublets` interface reports.\n68:\n69:`Neo4j_Batch` sends the `N` operations of an iteration as a list parameter\n70:and runs them with `UNWIND`, for example\n71:`UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l`. Neo4j finds each link of\n72:the list with the same index seek as the single statement. Update is two\n73:statements (to `(0, 0)` and back), every other operation one. Each All is\n74:already one statement, so it has no batch variant.\n75:\n76:The exact statements and data structures are documented in\n77:[`rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs`](rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs) and\n78:[`rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`](rust/src/doublets_impl.rs).\n79:\n80:## Method\n81:\n82:- `B` (background links) point links `1..=B` exist before every iteration, so\n83:  the indexes have a realistic size.\n84:- One iteration performs `N` (links per iteration) operations:\n85:\n86:  | Benchmark     | One iteration                                                  |\n87:  |---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|\n88:  | Create        | creates `N` links (ids `B + 1..=B + N`)                        |\n89:  | Update        | `N` × (`update(id, 0, 0)` and `update(id, id, id)`) = `2N` updates |\n90:  | Delete        | deletes links `B` down to `B - N + 1`                          |\n91:  | Each All      | one query that returns all `B` links                           |\n92:  | Each Identity, Each Concrete, Each Outgoing, Each Incoming | `N` queries, for ids `1..=N`, each returning one link |\n93:\n94:- The measured time of an iteration starts before the transaction begins and\n95:  ends after it is committed (for `Neo4j_Transaction`). After the measurement\n96:  the changes of the iteration are undone (Create is undone by deleting the\n97:  created links, Delete by creating them again), so every iteration starts\n98:  from the same links. The undo is not measured.\n99:- The background links are created once per benchmark and are not measured.\n100:- [Criterion.rs](https://github.com/bheisler/criterion.rs) collects the\n101:  samples: 10 samples (at least 5 s) for Neo4j, 100 samples for Doublets. The\n102:  tables show the median time of one iteration.\n103:- The CI runs the Neo4j and Doublets benchmarks in separate GitHub Actions jobs\n104:  (separate virtual machines), and each number of background links in its own\n105:  job, so they do not compete for the same CPU. Neo4j runs in the official\n106:  `neo4j:2026.09-community` Docker image without configuration changes.\n107:- Before the benchmarks, a test checks that all seven implementations return the\n108:  same results and that undoing an iteration restores the links\n109:  ([`rust/tests/same_behavior.rs`](rust/tests/same_behavior.rs)).\n110:\n111:Benchmarks on the main branch use `N = 1,000` and `B` = 10,000, 100,000 and\n112:1,000,000; such a run takes about 12 minutes on GitHub Actions (the longest\n113:job, Neo4j with 1,000,000 background links, about 11 minutes). Changes that do not\n116:touch the code, such as this README, start no tests or benchmarks.\n117:\n118:## Results\n119:\n120:The results below are generated by the CI on every change of the benchmark\n121:code on the main branch.         "type": "tool_result",
        "content": "# Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets\n\nThis repository measures how long basic operations on links take in two\ndatabases, with the same benchmarks written in two languages:\n\n| Language | Neo4j 2026.09 Community Edition (default settings)                     | Doublets (LinksPlatform, in the benchmark process)                                  |\n|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Rust     | [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs) Bolt driver             | [doublets](https://crates.io/crates/doublets) crate                                 |\n| C#       | official [Neo4j.Driver](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Neo4j.Driver)   | [Platform.Data.Doublets](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Platform.Data.Doublets) package |\n\nA link (doublet) is a triple `(id, source, target)`. In each language both\ndatabases implement the same interface (the [`Doublets`](https://docs.rs/doublets)\ntrait in Rust, [`IBenchedLinks`](csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets/IBenchedLinks.cs) in\nC#), and every benchmark calls the same methods on all of them. Both languages\nsend the same Cypher statements and run the same operations with the same\nsizes, so their results can be compared with each other.\n\nThe measured value is the time until an operation is finished from the point\nof view of the caller. Two workloads are reported:\n\n- **One operation per call**: every link operation is a separate call through\n  the `Doublets` interface, as an application calls it one at a time.\n- **Batch** (Neo4j only): the same operations of an iteration are sent to\n  Neo4j as one list in one Cypher statement, so the fixed cost of a statement\n  (round trips, query planning, commit) is paid once per iteration instead of\n  once per operation. Doublets has no batch calls; its batch work is the same\n  sequence of function calls as in the first workload.\n\n## What is compared\n\n| Implementation                | Where the data is                          | A finished operation is                            |\n|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `Doublets_United_Volatile`    | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n| `Doublets_United_NonVolatile` | memory-mapped file                         | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n| `Doublets_Split_Volatile`     | RAM of the benchmark process               | in RAM                                             |\n| `Doublets_Split_NonVolatile`  | two memory-mapped files                    | in the OS page cache (no `fsync`)                  |\n| `Neo4j_NonTransaction`        | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: every statement is its own transaction  |\n| `Neo4j_Transaction`           | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one explicit transaction per iteration  |\n| `Neo4j_Batch`                 | Neo4j server, reached over Bolt (TCP)      | committed: one statement with all `N` operations   |\n\n- **United** and **Split** are two Doublets storage layouts: link data and\n  index trees in one array, or in two separate arrays.\n- Neo4j can only be reached over the network, so every Neo4j operation\n  includes at least one round trip to the server. Doublets has no server: its\n  operations are function calls on the process memory. The comparison\n  therefore shows the cost of each way of storing links as it is used, not the\n  cost of the storage engines alone.\n- Neo4j writes every commit to its transaction log on disk. The Doublets stores\n  do not call `fsync`.\n\n## Operations\n\n| Operation     | `Doublets` method            | Neo4j (Cypher, one statement)                              | Doublets                                     |\n|---------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|\n| Create        | `create_point()`             | `CREATE (:Link {id: $id, source: $id, target: $id})`       | write the link, insert it into both trees    |\n| Update        | `update(id, source, target)` | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) ... SET l.source = ..., l.target = ...` | remove from both trees, write, insert  |\n| Delete        | `delete(id)`                 | `MATCH (l:Link {id: $id}) ... DELETE l`                    | remove from both trees, mark as free         |\n| Each All      | `each([*, *, *])`            | `MATCH (l:Link) RETURN ...`                                | scan the array                               |\n| Each Identity | `each_by([id, *, *])`        | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.id = $id RETURN ...`               | read array element `id`                      |\n| Each Concrete | `each_by([*, source, target])` | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.source = $source AND l.target = $target RETURN ...` | search the `(source, target)` tree |\n| Each Outgoing | `each_by([*, source, *])`    | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.source = $source RETURN ...`       | walk the `(source, target)` tree             |\n| Each Incoming | `each_by([*, *, target])`    | `MATCH (l:Link) WHERE l.target = $target RETURN ...`       | walk the `(target, source)` tree             |\n\nIn Neo4j a link is a node `(:Link {id, source, target})`. A link is found by\nits `id` property, which has a uniqueness constraint and therefore an index;\n`source` and `target` have indexes too. The internal node id (`elementId`) is\nnot used as the link id, because Neo4j chooses it itself and may reuse it,\nwhile link ids are chosen by the caller. Update and Delete are single\nstatements that also return the previous `source` and `target`, which the\n`Doublets` interface reports.\n\n`Neo4j_Batch` sends the `N` operations of an iteration as a list parameter\nand runs them with `UNWIND`, for example\n`UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l`. Neo4j finds each link of\nthe list with the same index seek as the single statement. Update is two\nstatements (to `(0, 0)` and back), every other operation one. Each All is\nalready one statement, so it has no batch variant.\n\nThe exact statements and data structures are documented in\n[`rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs`](rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs) and\n[`rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`](rust/src/doublets_impl.rs), and for C# in\n[`csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets/Neo4jLinks.cs`](csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets/Neo4jLinks.cs) and\n[`csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets/DoubletsLinks.cs`](csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets/DoubletsLinks.cs).\nThe C# names of the operations are `CreatePoint`, `Update`, `Delete` and\n`Each(id, source, target, visit)`.\n\n## Method\n\n- `B` (background links) point links `1..=B` exist before every iteration, so\n  the indexes have a realistic size.\n- One iteration performs `N` (links per iteration) operations:\n\n  | Benchmark     | One iteration                                                  |\n  |---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|\n  | Create        | creates `N` links (ids `B + 1..=B + N`)                        |\n  | Update        | `N` × (`update(id, 0, 0)` and `update(id, id, id)`) = `2N` updates |\n  | Delete        | deletes links `B` down to `B - N + 1`                          |\n  | Each All      | one query that returns all `B` links                           |\n  | Each Identity, Each Concrete, Each Outgoing, Each Incoming | `N` queries, for ids `1..=N`, each returning one link |\n\n- The measured time of an iteration starts before the transaction begins and\n  ends after it is committed (for `Neo4j_Transaction`). After the measurement\n  the changes of the iteration are undone (Create is undone by deleting the\n  created links, Delete by creating them again), so every iteration starts\n  from the same links. The undo is not measured.\n- The background links are created once per benchmark and are not measured.\n- [Criterion.rs](https://github.com/bheisler/criterion.rs) collects the\n  samples: 10 samples (at least 5 s) for Neo4j, 100 samples for Doublets. The\n  tables show the median time of one iteration.\n- The C# benchmarks sample the same way: their\n  [harness](csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets/Harness.cs) warms up and chooses the\n  number of iterations of every sample with the formulas of Criterion 0.8\n  (flat sampling for Neo4j, linear for Doublets), and prints the same\n  `bencher` lines (median and standard deviation), so one script reports both\n  languages.\n- The CI runs every language, database and number of background links in its\n  own GitHub Actions job (a separate virtual machine), so they do not compete\n  for the same CPU. Neo4j runs in the official `neo4j:2026.09-community`\n  Docker image without configuration changes.\n- Before the benchmarks, tests check that all seven implementations return the\n  same results and that undoing an iteration restores the links\n  ([`rust/tests/same_behavior.rs`](rust/tests/same_behavior.rs),\n  [`csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets.Tests/SameBehaviorTests.cs`](csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets.Tests/SameBehaviorTests.cs)).\n\nBenchmarks on the main branch use `N = 1,000` and `B` = 10,000, 100,000 and\n1,000,000; such a run takes about 12 minutes on GitHub Actions (the longest\njob, Neo4j with 1,000,000 background links, about 11 minutes). Pull requests\nrun a quick check with `N = 100` and `B = 1,000`. Larger `B` are not possible\nwith the Rust doublets 0.5.0 (see [Limitations](#limitations)). Changes that do not\ntouch the code, such as this README, start no tests or benchmarks.\n\n## Results\n\nThe results below are generated by the CI on every change of the benchmark\ncode on the main branch. Doublets has no batch calls, so its numbers are the same in both workloads.\n\nAdditional metrics (RAM, disk I/O, percentiles) are not part of this change. The README lists them as not measured; they can be added later as a separate report.\n\n## What changed in the method\n\n| Before | Now |\n|---|---|\n| Own HTTP client, a new TCP connection for every request, `Connection: close` | [neo4rs](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/neo4rs) 0.8 Bolt driver with default settings. Its connection pool is opened once and reused by all operations. |\n| Some operations sent two requests (an extra `MATCH` before `SET`/`DELETE`) | Every operation is one Cypher statement. Update and Delete return the previous `source`/`target` from the same statement. |\n| \"Transaction\" mode was not a real Neo4j transaction | `Neo4j_Transaction`: one explicit Bolt transaction per iteration, timed from `begin` to `commit`. `Neo4j_NonTransaction`: every statement is its own auto-commit transaction. |\n| No batch workload | `Neo4j_Batch`: `UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (l:Link {id: id}) DELETE l` and the same for Create, Update and the four `each_by` queries. `EXPLAIN` shows the same index seek per list element as the single statement. |\n| Background links were created again, one request per link, before every iteration, and deleted after it | Background links are created once per benchmark in batches (`UNWIND` + `CALL { ... } IN TRANSACTIONS OF 10000 ROWS`). The changes of an iteration are undone after the measurement, so every iteration starts from the same `B` links. Neither step is measured. |\n| Neo4j and Doublets ran in one job on one VM | Separate GitHub Actions jobs per backend and per `B` |\n\nThe official Neo4j drivers do not include Rust. neo4rs is the Bolt driver maintained in `neo4j-labs` and was accepted in the issue discussion. Its latest stable release is 0.8.0 (0.9 is only a release candidate).\n\n**\"Is it impossible to find a link by id in Neo4j?\"** No. A link is the node `(:Link {id, source, target})`, and it is found by the `id` property through the index of the uniqueness constraint. The internal `elementId` is not used as the link id, because Neo4j chooses it itself and may reuse it, while the caller chooses link ids. This is documented in the README and in `rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs`.\n\n## Code structure\n\n- `rust/src/neo4j_impl.rs`: `Doublets` implementation on top of neo4rs, plus the batch methods (`create_points_batch`, `update_batch`, `delete_batch`, `each_by_batch`). It documents every Cypher statement.\n- `rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`: documents the data structures of the Doublets stores and their capacity.\n- `rust/src/benched/`: setup, fork (background links) and undo for every implementation.\n- `rust/benches/`: one generic benchmark per operation, run by Criterion with `iter_custom`, so only the operations are timed; `benches/benchmarks/neo4j/batch.rs` holds the batch workload.\n- `rust/out.py`: generates the README tables and the charts in `Docs/` from the bencher output.\n- The old HTTP client (`client.rs`, `transaction.rs`, `exclusive.rs`) is removed.\n\n## Toolchain and dependencies\n\n- Latest stable Rust (`rust-toolchain.toml`: `stable`, 1.98.1 at the time of writing), edition 2024. `rustfmt.toml` had only nightly options and is removed; `out.py` parses them.\n- Actions: `checkout@v7`, `upload-artifact@v7`, `download-artifact@v8`, `setup-python@v7`.\n- The Dependabot alert for `atty` (from criterion 0.5 in the `main` lockfile) does not apply to this branch's lockfile and will close after the merge.\n\n## How the feedback is addressed\n\n| Feedback | Change |\n|---|---|\n| [Issue](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/issues/15): new TCP connection and HTTP request per operation, `Connection: close`, `bolt://` URI not used | neo4rs Bolt driver with one connection pool for the whole benchmark |\n| Issue: extra `MATCH` request before Update and Delete | one statement per operation; the previous values are returned by the same statement |\n| Issue: batching with `UNWIND` in one transaction | `Neo4j_Batch` column |\n| Issue: 10k → 100k → 1M → 10M → 100M links | `B` = 10k, 100k, 1M; larger sizes are blocked by the doublets 0.5.0 capacity bug (see Limitations) |\n| Issue: p50/p95/p99, RAM, disk I/O | not measured (README, Limitations); per the [vision](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/issues/15#issuecomment-5982246345) they belong in a separate report |\n| [kvkoval](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/issues/15#issuecomment-5982339792): maintained driver, pooled connections, normal transactions | neo4rs 0.8, pool reused, `Neo4j_Transaction` uses real Bolt transactions |\n| kvkoval: report single-operation latency and bulk throughput separately | two workloads, see Goal |\n| kvkoval: document any extra `MATCH` | Update and Delete use one `MATCH` to find the link by its indexed `id`; A `workflow_dispatch` run of this configuration ([run 37246154563](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/actions/runs/37246154563)) took about 12 minutes. The longest job, Neo4j with 1,000,000 links, took about 11 minutes. This is far below the 6-hour limit.\n- Neo4j uses 10 samples (at least 5 s) with flat sampling, Doublets uses 100 samples. Each benchmark id runs once per job.\n- Before the benchmarks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, and the tests:\n  - `rust/tests/same_behavior.rs`: all six implementations return the same results, undoing an iteration restores the links, and the Neo4j batch methods give the same links as the single operations;\n  - `rust/tests/doublets_capacity.rs`: the capacity limit described below.\n\n### No resources spent on changes outside of the code ([comment](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/pull/16#issuecomment-5982345541))\n\n- The workflow runs only for changes in `rust/**`, `rust-toolchain.toml` or the workflow file. The run in the screenshot was for the initial commit, before these filters existed.\n- For `pull_request` events GitHub applies these filters to **all** changes of the PR, so after one code change every later push, including README-only ones, ran the whole workflow. A new `changes` job (about 4 seconds) compares each push with the previous one and skips the tests and benchmarks if no code changed. Checked: README-only push → [run 37247227394](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/actions/runs/37247227394), all jobs skipped in 4 s.\n- Concurrency is set per job: a newer code run cancels the older one, but a skipped run does not cancel a code run that is still running (checked in the same test: [run 37247162816](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/actions/runs/37247162816) finished).\n- `--noplot`: Criterion does not draw its own HTML charts, which nobody reads in CI.\n\n### Fixed while testing: stale Criterion data from the cache\n\nrust-cache restored `target/criterion/<id>/base` directories without their files. Criterion then tried to compare every benchmark with this \"previous result\", printed an error inside the bencher line, and `out.py` showed N/A for every benchmark except the new `Neo4j_Batch` ones (runs 37244515815, 37245095420). Now:\n\n- every benchmark job uses a fresh `CRITERION_HOME` in `runner.temp`;\n- `out.py` stops with an error on any benchmark line without a time, so a broken run can never be published as N/A;\n- reproduction: `experiments/criterion-stale-baseline/run.sh` (log in `experiments/logs/criterion-stale-baseline.log`).\n\n## Limitations found (documented in the README)\n\n- **Driver round trips.** Measured with a counting TCP proxy (`experiments/bolt-round-trips`): neo4rs needs 3 round trips per statement in auto-commit mode and 2 inside a transaction. The `neo4j` crate needs 2 and 1.\n- **Capacity of doublets 0.5.0.** All four stores panic when link number 1,040,384 is created (\"Data part should be in data memory\" / \"Index part should be in index memory\"). After growing its memory, the store uses only the newly grown part as the whole array. The store starts with 8,192 links and grows to 2^20, so the capacity is 2^20 − 8,192 − 1 = 1,040,383 links.\n  - The upstream master branch has the same code.\n  - This is why `B` stops at 1,000,000. A 10,000,000 run was tried and reverted.\n  - The benchmark reports this limit as an error instead of panicking inside the store (`MAX_LINKS` in `rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`).\n  - Reproduction: `experiments/store-capacity`.\n- **Split store query bug in doublets 0.5.0.** After an `update`, links with `source != target` are not found by `[*, source, *]` / `[*, source, target]` (`experiments/split-store-bug`). The benchmarks use only point links and updates to `(0, 0)` and back, for which all stores agree.\n- **One client.** One thread, one operation (or one batch) at a time. Concurrent clients are not measured.\n- Results from before this PR are not comparable with the new ones, and the README no longer contains them.\n\n## Results of the full configuration (run 37246154563)\n\nMedian time of one iteration (1,000 operations, 2,000 for Update; Each All is one query over all links), in milliseconds, with `B = 1,000,000`. The NonVolatile Doublets stores are within a few percent of the Volatile ones.\n\n| Operation | Doublets United Volatile | Doublets Split Volatile | Neo4j NonTransaction | Neo4j Transaction | Neo4j Batch |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| Create | 0.113 | 0.051 | 990 | 302 | 8.1 |\n| Update | 0.517 | 0.039 | 1,760 | 625 | 63.7 |\n| Delete | 0.249 | 0.105 | 681 | 307 | 7.8 |\n| Each All | 2.7 | 7.0 | 2,576 | 2,612 | – |\n| Each Identity | 0.005 | 0.010 | 452 | 298 | 5.3 |\n| Each Concrete | 0.054 | 0.017 | 454 | 301 | 5.3 |\n| Each Outgoing | 0.060 | 0.014 | 450 | 300 | 5.2 |\n| Each Incoming | 0.108 | 0.017 | 450 | 300 | 5.5 |\n\nThe full tables and charts for all `B` and all seven implementations will be committed to the README by the CI after the merge.\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name neo4j -p 7687:7687 -e NEO4J_AUTH=neo…ord neo4j:2026.09-community\ncd rust\ncargo test --release -- --include-ignored\ncargo bench --bench bench\nBENCHMARK_LINKS=1000 BENCHMARK_BACKGROUND_LINKS=1000000 cargo bench --bench bench\n```\n\nThe experiments and their logs are in `experiments/` (see `experiments/README.md`).\n\n<!-- hive-mind:changes:start -->\n### Changes\n- 74 file(s) modified\n- 6533 line(s) added\n- 3079 line(s) removed\n- Files:\n  - The run in the screenshot was for the initial commit, before these filters existed.\n- For `pull_request` events GitHub applies these filters to **all** changes of the PR, so after one code change every later push, including README-only ones, ran the whole workflow. A new `changes` job (about 4 seconds) compares each push with the previous one and skips the tests and benchmarks if no code changed. Checked: README-only push → [run 37247227394](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/actions/runs/37247227394), all jobs skipped in 4 s.\n- Concurrency is set per job: a newer code run cancels the older one, but a skipped run does not cancel a code run that is still running (checked in the same test: [run 37247162816](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/actions/runs/37247162816) finished).\n- `--noplot`: Criterion does not draw its own HTML charts, which nobody reads in CI.\n\n### Fixed while testing: stale Criterion data from the cache\n\nrust-cache restored `target/criterion/<id>/base` directories without their files. Criterion then tried to compare every benchmark with this \"previous result\", printed an error inside the bencher line, and `out.py` showed N/A for every benchmark except the new `Neo4j_Batch` ones (runs 37244515815, 37245095420). Now:\n\n- every benchmark job uses a fresh `CRITERION_HOME` in `runner.temp`;\n- `out.py` stops with an error on any benchmark line without a time, so a broken run can never be published as N/A;\n- reproduction: `experiments/criterion-stale-baseline/run.sh` (log in `experiments/logs/criterion-stale-baseline.log`).\n\n## Limitations found (documented in the README)\n\n- **Driver round trips.** Measured with a counting TCP proxy (`experiments/bolt-round-trips`): neo4rs needs 3 round trips per statement in auto-commit mode and 2 inside a transaction. The `neo4j` crate needs 2 and 1.\n- **Capacity of doublets 0.5.0.** All four stores panic when link number 1,040,384 is created (\"Data part should be in data memory\" / \"Index part should be in index memory\"). After growing its memory, the store uses only the newly grown part as the whole array. The store starts with 8,192 links and grows to 2^20, so the capacity is 2^20 − 8,192 − 1 = 1,040,383 links.\n  - The upstream master branch has the same code.\n  - This is why `B` stops at 1,000,000. A 10,000,000 run was tried and reverted.\n  - The benchmark reports this limit as an error instead of panicking inside the store (`MAX_LINKS` in `rust/src/doublets_impl.rs`).\n  - Reproduction: `experiments/store-capacity`.\n- **Split store query bug in doublets 0.5.0.** After an `update`, links with `source != target` are not found by `[*, source, *]` / `[*, source, target]` (`experiments/split-store-bug`). The benchmarks use only point links and updates to `(0, 0)` and back, for which all stores agree.\n- **One client.** One thread, one operation (or one batch) at a time. Concurrent clients are not measured.\n- Results from before this PR are not comparable with the new ones, and the README no longer contains them.\n\n## Results of the full configuration (run 37246154563)\n\nMedian time of one iteration (1,000 operations, 2,000 for Update; Each All is one query over all links), in milliseconds, with `B = 1,000,000`. The NonVolatile Doublets stores are within a few percent of the Volatile ones.\n\n| Operation | Doublets United Volatile | Doublets Split Volatile | Neo4j NonTransaction | Neo4j Transaction | Neo4j Batch |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| Create | 0.113 | 0.051 | 990 | 302 | 8.1 |\n| Update | 0.517 | 0.039 | 1,760 | 625 | 63.7 |\n| Delete | 0.249 | 0.105 | 681 | 307 | 7.8 |\n| Each All | 2.7 | 7.0 | 2,576 | 2,612 | – |\n| Each Identity | 0.005 | 0.010 | 452 | 298 | 5.3 |\n| Each Concrete | 0.054 | 0.017 | 454 | 301 | 5.3 |\n| Each Outgoing | 0.060 | 0.014 | 450 | 300 | 5.2 |\n| Each Incoming | 0.108 | 0.017 | 450 | 300 | 5.5 |\n\nThe full tables and charts for all `B` and all seven implementations will be committed to the README by the CI after the merge.\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name neo4j -p 7687:7687 -e NEO4J_AUTH=neo…ord neo4j:2026.09-community\ncd rust\ncargo test --release -- --include-ignored\ncargo bench --bench bench\nBENCHMARK_LINKS=1000 BENCHMARK_BACKGROUND_LINKS=1000000 cargo bench --bench bench\n```\n\nThe experiments and their logs are in `experiments/` (see `experiments/README.md`).\n\n<!-- hive-mind:changes:start -->\n### Changes\n- 74 file(s) modified\n- 6533 line(s) added\n- 3079 line(s) removed\n- Files:\n  - Study: Upgrade to Latest `doublets-rs` and Switch to Stable Rust (Issue #23)\n\n## Summary\n\nThe `Comparisons.PostgreSQLVSDoublets` benchmark project depended on an old,\npre-release, **git-pinned** build of [`doublets-rs`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n(`0.1.0-pre+beta.15`) and required the **nightly** Rust toolchain\n(`nightly-2022-08-22`). The nightly pin was needed because that version of\n`doublets` relied on unstable language features (`allocator_api`,\n`generic_associated_types`, and the `Try` trait for `?` on a custom control-flow\ntype).\n\nMeanwhile, upstream `doublets-rs` released **v0.3.0** (2026-04-18), which is\npublished on crates.io and — most importantly — **migrated from nightly to\nstable Rust (1.85+)**.     1\t# Comparisons.SpacetimeDBVSDoublets\n     2\t\n     3\tBenchmark comparing [SpacetimeDB 2](https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB) vs [Doublets](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs) performance for basic CRUD operations with links.\n     4\t\n     5\tSpacetimeDB is benchmarked using the official `spacetimedb-sdk` Rust crate connected to a running SpacetimeDB 2.0 server. Doublets is benchmarked with both in-memory (volatile) and file-backed (non-volatile) storage variants.\n     6\t\n     7\t## Benchmark Operations\n     8\t\n     9\t| Operation | Description |\n    10\t|---|---|\n    11\t| Create | Create a self-referential point link (id == source == target) |\n    12\t| Delete | Delete links by id |\n    13\t| Update | Update link source and target |\n    14\t| Query All | Retrieve all links (`[*, *, *]`) |\n    15\t| Query by Id | Retrieve a link by id |\n    16\t| Query by Source | Retrieve all links with a given source |\n    17\t| Query by Target | Retrieve all links with a given target |\n    18\t\n    19\t## Backends Benchmarked\n    20\t\n    21\t### SpacetimeDB\n    22\t- **SpacetimeDB** — connects to a running SpacetimeDB 2.0 server via the official `spacetimedb-sdk` Rust crate; uses the `links` table defined in the `spacetime-module` WebAssembly module\n    23\t\n    24\tThe benchmark uses the official SpacetimeDB Rust client SDK, calling reducers to mutate data and reading from the client-side subscription cache.\n    25\t\n    26\t### Doublets\n    27\t- **Doublets United Volatile** — in-memory store; links stored as contiguous `(index, source, target)` units\n    28\t- **Doublets Split Volatile** — in-memory store; separate data and index memory regions\n    29\t- **Doublets United NonVolatile** — file-backed store; same contiguous layout but memory-mapped to a single file; data persists to disk\n    30\t- **Doublets Split NonVolatile** — file-backed store; separate data and index files; both memory-mapped; data persists to disk\n    31\t\n    32\tDoublets uses a recursive-less size-balanced tree for O(1) lookup by id and O(log n + k) traversal by source/target. The file-backed variants use `memmap2` for memory-mapped file I/O, flushing changes to disk on drop via `sync_all()`. See [`rust/doublets-patched/PATCHES.md`](rust/doublets-patched/PATCHES.md) for why a local patched copy is used instead of the published crates.io version.\n    33\t\n    34\t## Benchmark Background\n    35\t\n    36\tEach benchmark iteration pre-populates the database with background links to simulate a realistic database state:\n    37\t\n    38\t- **Background links**: `BACKGROUND_LINK_COUNT` (default: 3000) — already present before measurement\n    39\t- **Benchmark links**: `BENCHMARK_LINK_COUNT` (default: 1000) — the operations being measured\n    40\t\n    41\t## Results\n    42\t\n    43\tThe numbers below represent the amount of time (ns) a single benchmark iteration takes.\n    44\t\n    45\t- The first chart shows time in a pixel (linear) scale. Doublets bars are drawn with a\n    46\t  minimum visible width, otherwise they would not be visible next to SpacetimeDB.\n    47\t- The second chart shows time in a logarithmic scale, to see the difference clearly,\n    48\t  because it is around 3-5 orders of magnitude.\n    49\t\n    50\tCharts and the table are recalculated by the\n    51\t[Rust Benchmark workflow](.github/workflows/rust-benchmark.yml) on every push to `main`\n    52\tand committed back to this repository, so the results are visible here without running\n    53\tthe benchmark locally.\n    54\t\n    55\t### Rust\n    56\t\n    57\t![Image of Rust benchmark (pixel   77\tSpacetimeDB for the same operation.\n    78\t\n    79\t## Conclusion\n    80\t\n    81\tDoublets is an embedded store: an operation is a few pointer dereferences and tree\n    82\trotations in memory (or in a memory-mapped file), while every SpacetimeDB operation is a\n    83\treducer call over a WebSocket connection to a separate process, and every query is served\n    84\tfrom the client-side subscription cache. The measured difference is dominated by that\n    85\tarchitectural difference rather than by the data structures themselves.\n    86\t\n    87\tTo get fresh numbers, please fork the repository and rerun the benchmark in GitHub Actions.\n    88\t\n    89\t## Operation Complexity\n    90\t\n    91\t| Operation | SpacetimeDB | Doublets United | Doublets Split |\n    92\t|---|---|---|---|\n    93\t| Create | O(log n) + network | O(log n) | O(log n) |\n    94\t| Delete | O(log n) + network | O(log n) | O(log n) |\n    95\t| Update | O(log n) + network | O(log n) | O(log n) |\n    96\t| Query All | O(n) cache read | O(n) | O(n) |\n    97\t| Query by Id | O(n) cache scan | O(1) | O(1) |\n    98\t| Query by Source | O(n) cache scan | O(log n + k) | O(log n + k) |\n    99\t| Query by Target | O(n) cache scan | O(log n + k) | O(log n + k) |\n   100\t\n   101\tThe algorithmic complexity is the same for volatile and non-volatile Doublets variants. The non-volatile variants have additional I/O overhead due to memory-mapped file writes (flushed to disk on drop).\n   102\t\n   103\t## Related Benchmarks\n   104\t\n   105\t- [Neo4j vs 139\t- The split stores of doublets 0.5.0 (Rust) lose a link that is updated to\n   140\t  reference itself, so the benchmark updates a link to `(0, 0)` first, which\n   141\t  is the state links are ([experiments/csharp_split_linked_list](experiments/csharp_split_linked_list)).\n   160\t- Objects stores use external references for numbers and Unicode symbols, so\n   161\t  raw values never #17.\n\n## Goal\n\nMake the generated README results readable at a glance again. Each Doublets result should show how many times faster or slower it is than Neo4j, as the earlier benchmarks did. The repository should also follow the best practices of the sibling comparison repositories and support both a Rust and a C# version. The practices missing in the sibling repositories are reported there as issues (see below).\n\n## Changes\n\n| Before | Now |\n|---|---|\n| Doublets cells showed only the time, so the reader had to compare `79.8 µs` with `10.2 ms` themselves | Every Doublets cell shows its ratio to the fastest Neo4j implementation of the operation (in **bold**), for example `79.8 µs (128× faster)`, `(N× slower)`, or `(≈ same)` when the medians differ by less than 5% or their ±1 standard deviation ranges overlap |\n| `rust/out.py`: no tests, parsed only the median | `scripts/benchmark_report.py` parses the median and the deviation. It rejects input that cannot be published: error lines without a time, unknown benchmarks or file names, missing results, or a missing backend. It replaces only the text between `<!-- results:start -->` and `<!-- results:end -->`. It has 26 unit tests in `scripts/test_benchmark_report.py`, which CI runs |\n| Tables did not say where the numbers came from | A line above every table gives the Neo4j version and edition, the driver and Doublets library versions (read from `Cargo.lock` and the `.csproj`), the CPU, the date and a link to the GitHub Actions run. `scripts/benchmark_header.sh` writes this metadata into each result file |\n| Rust only | **C# version** in `csharp/`: .NET 10 with the official [Neo4j.Driver](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Neo4j.Driver) 6.3.0 and [Platform.Data.Doublets](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Platform.Data.Doublets) 0.18.1. It has the same seven implementations, the same Cypher statements, operations, sizes and undo steps as Rust |\n| — | `### Rust` and `### C#` sections in the README, each with tables plus linear and log charts for every `B` (`Docs/bench_<language>_<B>.png`, `Docs/bench_<language>_log_scale_<B>.png`) |\n| `rust.yml`, Rust jobs only | `benchmarks.yml`. A `test-csharp` job runs `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, a build with warnings as errors, and `dotnet test` against Neo4j. The benchmark jobs are a `language × B` matrix, and one report job builds the README from all languages. The path filters and the `changes` job include `csharp/**` |\n\n### The C# version\n\n- `IBenchedLinks` is the C# counterpart of the `Doublets` trait as the benchmarks use it: `CreatePoint`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Each(id, source, target, visit)` and `Count`, plus `Fork`/`Unfork` for the background links and `Begin`/`Commit` for transactions.\n- `Benchmarks.cs` describes every operation once. All stores run exactly the same sequence of calls, the same way the generic Rust benchmarks do.\n- `Harness.cs` mirrors Criterion 0.8, so both languages are measured the same way:\n  - The warm-up doubles the iteration count until the warm-up time is reached.\n  - Iterations per sample follow Criterion's flat formula (Neo4j: 10 samples, 5 s) or linear formula (Doublets: 100 samples, 2 s).\n  - Only `Begin` + operation + `Commit` is timed; the undo is not.\n  - The output is the median and standard deviation as a `bencher` line (`test Create/Neo4j_Transaction ... bench: 44,055,505 ns/iter (+/- 5,345,991)`), so one report script reads both languages.\n- Tests (`csharp/Neo4jVSDoublets.Tests`, xUnit v3), the same checks as `rust/tests/same_behavior.rs`:\n  - All seven implementations return the same links.\n  - Undoing every benchmark's work restores the background links.\n  - The Neo4j batch methods give the same results as the single operations and fail on missing links.\n  - The harness's iteration counts, statistics and output format match Criterion.\n  - Without `NEO4J_URI`, the Neo4j tests are skipped.\n\n## How the issue is addressed\n\n| Requirement | Change |\n|---|---|\n| \"Show how many times faster or slower, as it was in previous benchmarks\" | `(N× faster)` / `(N× slower)` / `(≈ same)` in every Doublets cell, relative to the fastest Neo4j implementation of the operation. The numbers are factual ratios without rating words, as required by the [vision in #15](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/issues/15#issuecomment-5982246345), and noise is not claimed as a difference |\n| \"Sync best practices with SQLite, SpacetimeDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, DeepGqlStandard\" | Taken from the siblings: ratio annotations, the `≈ same` threshold, generated sections between markers, linear + log charts, provenance, tested report generator, a C# version next to Rust. The siblings lack practices that this repository has (path filters with the `changes` job, per-job concurrency and timeouts, a pinned database image, same-behavior tests, PR quick runs). Those gaps are reported in: [SQLiteVSDoublets#113](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.SQLiteVSDoublets/issues/113), [SpacetimeDBVSDoublets#16](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.SpacetimeDBVSDoublets/issues/16), [PostgreSQLVSDoublets#42](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.PostgreSQLVSDoublets/issues/42), [RedisVSDoublets#4](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.RedisVSDoublets/issues/4), [DeepGqlStandard#4](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.DeepGqlStandard/issues/4) |\n| \"Support Rust and C# versions\" | Both are implemented, tested in CI, benchmarked by CI, and reported in the README |\n| Requirements of earlier issues (#5, #15) | Still met: benchmarks run only for code changes, per-backend and per-`B` jobs, background links and undo not measured, Bolt driver with pooled connections, the batch workload, the 6-hour budget. No existing feature was removed (`rust/out.py` is replaced by `scripts/benchmark_report.py`) |\n\n## CI and time budget\n\n- The PR quick check (`N = 100`, `B = 1,000`, Rust and C#) took about 7 minutes in [run 37518265091](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/actions/runs/37518265091), and every job passed:\n  - `test` (Rust fmt, clippy and tests, plus the report tests): 1m 52s;\n  - `test-csharp`: 1m 13s, with 14 tests passed and none skipped;\n  - the four benchmark jobs: 2m 22s to 4m 14s;\n  - `report`: 23s.\n- On `main`, the C# jobs run in parallel with the Rust jobs (12 benchmark jobs, each with a 120-minute timeout). The longest Rust job (Neo4j with B = 1,000,000) took 8m 39s (13 minutes for the whole run) in [run 37293828831](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.Neo4jVSDoublets/actions/runs/37293828831). The C# jobs repeat the same work and sampling, so a similar time is expected. This could not be measured before the merge: `workflow_dispatch` only starts workflows whose file exists on the default branch, and the workflow is renamed to `benchmarks.yml` here. Locally, C# Doublets Create with B = 1,000,000 ran in about 1 minute on a loaded 6-core machine. The slowest Neo4j benchmark, Each All with B = 1,000,000 (`N = 1,000`), took 12.0 s per iteration in C# and 15.8 s in Rust when run one after the other against the same local server. So the C# Neo4j jobs should take about as long as the Rust ones.\n- Changes outside `rust/`, `csharp/`, `scripts/`, `rust-toolchain.toml` and the workflow still start no tests or benchmarks.\n\n### Results of the PR run (`B = 1,000`, `N = 100`)\n\n| Operation | Rust: Doublets Split Volatile | Rust: Neo4j Batch | C#: Doublets Split Volatile | C#: Neo4j Batch |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| Create | 5.14 µs (482× faster) | 2.48 ms | 17.2 µs (146× faster) | 2.51 ms |\n| Update | 3.94 µs (1,030× faster) | 4.05 ms | 13.7 µs (347× faster) | 4.75 ms |\n| Delete | 10.7 µs (174× faster) | 1.87 ms | 15.6 µs (133× faster) | 2.07 ms |\n| Each Identity | 999 ns (1,020× faster) | 1.02 ms | 5.97 µs (231× faster) | 1.38 ms |\n\nThe Neo4j columns of the two languages are close: both send the same statements to the same server image. The C# Doublets stores (Platform.Data.Doublets 0.18.1) take 1.5–6× as long as the Rust ones (doublets 0.5.0). This is a difference between the libraries, not between the harnesses.\n\n## Limitations\n\n- The C# results section shows `_No results yet._` until the first CI run on `main` commits its tables and charts. The Rust tables in this PR are regenerated from the existing `main` data. That data was measured before the metadata header existed, so its CPU is shown as `unknown`.\n- Neo4j publishes no official Rust driver, so Rust uses neo4rs and C# uses the official driver. The two drivers make a different number of network round trips per statement, so the Neo4j columns of the two languages are not expected to be equal.\n- The B = 1,000,000 limit comes from the Rust doublets 0.5.0 capacity bug. The C# stores ran Create with B = 1,000,000 locally without problems, and C# keeps the same sizes so the two languages can be compared.\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name neo4j -p 7687:7687 -p 7474:7474 -e NEO4J_AUTH=neo…ord neo4j:2026.09-community\npython3 -m unittest discover -s scripts                    # report generator\n(cd rust && cargo test --release -- --include-ignored)\n(cd csharp && NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:7687 dotnet test)\n# results/<rust|csharp>-<B>-<neo4j|doublets>.txt, then:\npython3 scripts/benchmark_report.py results --readme README.md --charts Docs\n```\n\nThe README's \"Running locally\" section has the full
